To overcome this challenge, we developed hollow hydrogel fibers using microfluidic coaxial printing, which were then seeded with human coronary artery smooth muscle cells (HCASMCs) and human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) to generate a biomimetic coronary artery construct. The physiological responsiveness of the model was validated through stimulation with TNF-α, and a KD-specific pathological model was established by introducing serum from KD patients. Using this biomimetic platform, we evaluated the therapeutic potential of Atorvastatin (ATOR) and the NLRP3 inflammasome inhibitor MCC950, and explored their underlying mechanisms in attenuating vascular inflammation. Overall, this work introduces a structurally relevant in vitro platform that offers new opportunities for studying KD pathogenesis and accelerating the development of targeted therapies.

title: Type II collagen as a material-mediated instructive platform: Cartilage regeneration and fibrosis suppression via the Tp63–Cytl1 axis
abstract: A major challenge in cartilage regeneration is maintaining the hyaline cartilage phenotype and matrix over time while limiting hypertrophy and fibrosis. Here, type II collagen (Col2)-hyaluronic acid (Col2H) and type I collagen-hyaluronic acid (Col1H) sponges were compared using long-term three-dimensional chondrocyte culture, cross-species transcriptomic analysis, and functional experiments. Col2H supported longer-term chondrocyte phenotype and matrix retention than Col1H. Cytl1 was prioritized because it ranked highly in Col2H-associated analysis and was consistently downregulated during chondrocyte dedifferentiation in human and rat datasets. Functional assays, ChIP-qPCR, and co-immunoprecipitation supported involvement of an Itgb8-Nov-Tp63-Cytl1 regulatory network in the Col2-associated response. Col2H also showed preliminary cartilage-repair potential in a rabbit defect model. In human osteoarthritis cartilage, a five-gene signature comprising Cytl1, Tp63, Nov, Itgb8, and TIMP3 showed internal stability and an association with histological severity. These findings support a material-associated regulatory role for Col2H in chondrocyte phenotype and matrix maintenance.

title: Shape-dependent transmembrane transport of mesenchymal stem cell membrane-coated mesoporous silica nanoparticles enhances anti-glioma therapy
abstract: The blood-brain barrier (BBB) remains a major obstacle to effective glioma chemotherapy, and although mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) membrane (MSCM) coated nanoparticles offer a biomimetic strategy for glioma-targeted delivery, the role of particle morphology in such systems remains unclear. Herein, doxorubicin-loaded mesoporous silica nanoparticles coated with MSC membranes (MSCM@MSN@DOX) were developed with three morphologies-spherical (AR∼1), short rod-shaped (AR∼1.5), and long rod-shaped (AR∼3) to study the shape effect of MSC biomimetic drug delivery system on glioma treatment. All formulations showed successful membrane coating, retention of MSC-associated proteins, and comparable drug loading, release, and stability, enabling assessment of shape-dependent delivery behavior. Compared with AR∼1 and AR∼1.5 counterparts, AR∼3 particles exhibited enhanced motility, higher uptake by bEnd.3 and GL261 cells, improved trans-BBB transport, and deeper tumor spheroid penetration. Mechanistic studies suggested that these effects were associated with stronger nanoparticle-cell membrane interactions and morphology-dependent endocytic behavior. In an intracranial GL261 glioma model, AR∼3 particles achieved greater brain/glioma-region accumulation, more pronounced tumor growth inhibition, and extended survival, with no overt systemic toxicity under the tested regimen. These findings identify particle morphology as an important optimization parameter within the investigated MSC membrane-coated MSN system and provide a basis for shape optimization of this biomimetic nanocarrier platform for brain-targeted drug delivery.

title: A core-shell microneedle patch coordinates early anti-inflammatory modulation and sustained pro-angiogenic stimulation for cardiac repair after myocardial infarction
abstract: Myocardial infarction (MI) involves a temporally evolving pathological cascade, in which acute NLRP3 inflammasome-mediated inflammation and insufficient reparative angiogenesis sequentially contribute to adverse ventricular remodeling. However, most current therapies lack the spatiotemporal control needed to match these evolving therapeutic demands. Here, we developed a core-shell microneedle (MN)-based epicardial patch for spatiotemporally programmed MI treatment through sequential delivery of the NLRP3 inhibitor MCC950 and basic fibroblast growth factor (bFGF). The rapidly hydrating methacrylated hyaluronic acid (HAMA) shell enabled early release of MCC950 to suppress acute inflammatory injury, whereas the chitosan-based core and backing layer provided sustained bFGF release to support later angiogenesis. The resulting HAMA/CS MN patch exhibited a well-defined core-shell architecture, suitable mechanical strength, excellent cytocompatibility, and differentiated release behavior. In vitro , MCC950-loaded MN patches effectively suppressed oxygen-glucose deprivation-induced suppressed activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome, lowered the expression levels of caspase-1, IL-1β, and IL-18, and attenuated cardiomyocyte apoptosis. Meanwhile, sustained bFGF release substantially improved endothelial cell proliferation, migration, and tube formation. In a rat MI model, epicardial implantation of the dual-loaded MN patch reduced inflammatory activation, enhanced angiogenesis, decreased fibrosis, and showed greater preservation of cardiac function relative to untreated MI or single-agent controls. These findings demonstrate that core-shell MN-mediated sequential local delivery can align therapeutic kinetics with post-MI pathophysiology. This study provides a localized and programmable platform for cardiac repair and potentially for other dynamic inflammatory-regenerative diseases.

title: A bacteria-releasing mucoadhesive sheet for localized delivery and penetrative therapy of gastrointestinal cancer
abstract: Bacteria-based cancer therapy shows promise for solid tumors, but effective localization and long-term retention in the gastrointestinal (GI) tract remain limited by peristalsis and fluid flow. We developed a Bacteria-Releasing Mucoadhesive Sheet (BRMS), a deployable multilayered platform for precise localized, active bacterial delivery. The BRMS consists of three functional layers: an unrolling layer for rapid deployment and conformal adhesion to the mucosa; a guard layer to minimize bacterial loss and enforce unidirectional release; and a therapeutic layer loaded with engineered Salmonella secreting the anticancer protein VC1. In its rolled state, the BRMS is compatible with delivery via standard endoscopes or capsule robots. Upon deployment, it protects bacteria from the luminal environment, prolongs local retention, and promotes penetration into deep tumor tissue. We validated its spatiotemporally controlled delivery and deployment through ex vivo experiments. In a CT-26 colon cancer mouse model, the BRMS achieved robust tumor growth inhibition and regression without detectable systemic toxicity. In conclusion, the BRMS is a novel bacterial delivery platform that overcomes GI physiological barriers, enabling sustained bacterial infiltration into deep tumor regions, and offering a powerful strategy to extend the therapeutic potential of bacteria-based cancer therapies.

title: Oxygen-augmented erythrocyte-liposome hybrids to overcome paclitaxel resistance in triple-negative breast cancer metastasis via enhanced ferroptosis
abstract: Paclitaxel (PTX) resistance in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is closely associated with ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporters-medicated drug efflux and hypoxia-driven upregulation of hypoxia-inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α), which together promote tumor progression and metastasis. Although blood transfusion or hyperbaric oxygen therapy can partially alleviate systemic hypoxia, neither approach effectively relieves chemoresistance driven by intratumoral hypoxia. To address this challenge, we have developed a biomimetic hybrid delivery system (red blood cell hitchhiking-liposomes encapsulate hemoglobin and paclitaxel, RBC-LEHP) that utilizes red blood cell-hitchhiking technology along with pH-responsive liposomes, to co-deliver hemoglobin (Hb) and PTX to overcome hypoxia-associated chemoresistance. This system achieves dual-stage targeting: passive sequestration in pulmonary metastatic lesions through erythrocyte hitchhiking and active tumor internalization mediated by pH-sensitive DOPE phospholipids. Our study revealed that RBC-LEHP effectively alleviated the hypoxia microenvironment through Hb-mediated oxygenation upon tumor cellular internalization and downregulated HIF-1α and glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4), while simultaneously enhancing reactive oxygen species (ROS)-mediated lipid peroxidation to induce ferroptosis. This amplified oxidative stress further triggered mitochondrial dysfunction, suppressed P-glycoprotein (P-gp)-mediated PTX efflux, reversed PTX resistance, and promoted apoptotic cell death. In vivo results confirmed that RBC-LEHP-mediated therapeutic cascade of “lung targeted delivery → hypoxia alleviation → ferroptosis/chemotherapy → tumor suppression” significantly enhanced antitumor efficacy against TNBC. This biomimetic platform provides a promising strategy for overcoming physiological barriers and chemoresistance in metastatic TNBC therapy.

title: Electroacupuncture synergizes with anti-ferroptosis bioelectrical niche remodeling to promote spinal cord regeneration
abstract: Severe spinal cord injury (SCI) frequently causes persistent neurological deficits, and its repair is constrained by multiple pathological factors including deterioration of the microenvironment following secondary injury, massive neuronal loss, interruption of electrical signal conduction, and insufficient endogenous regenerative capacity. Although electroacupuncture (EA) participates in the rehabilitation of SCI by regulating inflammatory responses and promoting the secretion of neurotrophic factors, standalone EA therapy can hardly fully reverse oxidative stress, ferroptosis and neural circuit destruction following severe SCI. Accordingly, this study constructs a conductive anti-ferroptosis hydrogel system (HBP@BMSCs), which utilizes dopamine-grafted hyaluronic acid (HADA) as the bionic matrix, baicalin-polypyrrole (BA-PPy) as the functional component, and is loaded with bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs). This hydrogel system is combined with EA for the repair of severe SCI. The results demonstrate that the HBP hydrogel exhibits favorable cytocompatibility, which can support the survival of BMSCs and maintain their typical mesenchymal stem cell phenotype. In vitro experiments demonstrate that HBP hydrogel effectively alleviates TBHP-induced oxidative stress injury and Erastin-induced ferroptosis-related injury, and exerts a protective effect on BMSCs and PC12 cells. In vivo experiments further confirmed that the combination therapy of HBP@BMSCs with EA significantly downregulated the expression levels of 4HNE, COX2, NOX2, FTH, FTL and TFR after SCI, and restored the expression levels of XCT, GPX4, SOD1 and FPN, thereby alleviating ROS accumulation, lipid peroxidation, iron overload and ferroptosis. With the alleviation of oxidative stress and ferroptosis-related secondary damage, the combination therapy further downregulates the expression of Bax and C-caspase3, upregulates Bcl-2 levels, and significantly inhibits neuronal apoptosis. In addition, the BA-PPy conductive network can synergize with EA to enhance electrical stimulation conduction, upregulate NGF/NGFR and BDNF neurotrophic signaling pathways, and promote the neural lineage differentiation of BMSCs, axon regeneration, corticospinal tract (CST) remodeling, and the recovery of motor function. In conclusion, HBP@BMSCs combined with EA exerts multiple synergistic effects including microenvironment remodeling, anti-ferroptosis protection, stem cell delivery and electroactive neural regeneration, providing a comprehensive therapeutic strategy with translational potential for severe SCI repair.

title: Adhesive cationic hyaluronic acid loading with small extracellular vesicles from IL-6 activated mesenchymal stem cells improves repair of corrosive esophageal injury
abstract: The treatment of corrosive esophageal injury (CEI) remains challenging due to recurrent courses, frequent complications, and severe tissue damage. Enhancing the therapeutic potential of mesenchymal stem cell-derived small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) through cytokine preconditioning has emerged as a promising strategy. In this study, functionally enhanced sEVs (E-sEVs) were generated by pretreating umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stem cells with interleukin-6 (IL-6). E-sEVs exhibited superior capabilities in promoting fibroblast migration and suppressing macrophage-mediated inflammation compared to naïve sEVs. To improve local retention and therapeutic efficacy, E-sEVs were integrated into a cationic hyaluronic acid (CHA) hydrogel with strong bioadhesive properties, forming a composite system termed E-sEVs@CHA. In vitro assays demonstrated that E-sEVs@CHA effectively promoted endothelial cell invasion, exhibited antioxidant activity, and modulated macrophage polarization toward an anti-inflammatory phenotype. In a rat model of CEI, E-sEVs@CHA significantly reduced esophageal inflammation, oxidative stress, and fibrotic remodeling, leading to improved tissue repair and reduced stricture formation. This study presents a novel cell-free therapeutic strategy with translational potential for the management of corrosive esophageal injury.

title: A hypoxia-responsive calixarene supramolecular system enables redox-regulated matrix remodeling for postmenopausal osteoporosis
abstract: Postmenopausal osteoporosis (PMOP) is characterized by progressive bone loss driven by excessive osteoclast activity, impaired osteogenesis, and maladaptive remodeling of the bone microenvironment. Although raloxifene (RLX) is clinically approved for PMOP, its therapeutic potential is constrained by limited bone selectivity and systemic adverse effects. Here, we report a hypoxia-responsive, bone-targeted supramolecular system (RLX@PnAC4A) that integrates site-selective drug delivery with redox regulation to enable coordinated matrix remodeling within the osteoporotic niche. PnAC4A was engineered through azobenzene functionalization and phosphonate modification, endowing the calixarene host with hypoxia-triggered reducibility, high-affinity bone targeting, and efficient RLX encapsulation. The resulting supramolecular assemblies exhibited stable host-guest interactions and selective drug release under hypoxic conditions. In vitro, RLX@PnAC4A preferentially restored intracellular redox homeostasis under hypoxic and inflammatory stress, enhanced osteogenic differentiation, and suppressed osteoclastogenesis in a microenvironment-dependent manner. Following systemic administration in ovariectomized (OVX) mice, RLX@PnAC4A rapidly accumulated in bone tissue and significantly improved trabecular microarchitecture, bone formation dynamics, and structural integrity compared with free RLX. Transcriptomic profiling further revealed that OVX induced a broadly immune-activated disease program, whereas PnAC4A alone established an extracellular matrix-associated conditioning state. Importantly, RLX@PnAC4A activated a dominant, therapy-specific transcriptional module enriched in extracellular matrix remodeling and pro-regenerative signaling, accompanied by directional rescue of key disease-associated nodes. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that RLX@PnAC4A functions as an active supramolecular regulator, exerting therapeutic efficacy through a hierarchically organized transcriptional architecture that couples bone targeting, redox modulation, and osteoblast-osteoclast coordination. This hypoxia -responsive calixarene platform establishes a mechanistically grounded strategy for precision intervention in postmenopausal osteoporosis.

title: Cartilage-targeting engineered probiotic bacterial extracellular vesicles treat osteoarthritis through modulation of matrix homeostasis
abstract: Reversing extracellular matrix (ECM) metabolic dysregulation to facilitate cartilage repair represents a key therapeutic strategy for osteoarthritis (OA) treatment. Owing to the avascular nature of joint structures, intra-articular injection is a commonly used clinical administration route. However, the current drug retention time is insufficient to effectively reverse OA progression. In this study, we demonstrated that natural bacterial extracellular vesicles (BEVs) are capable of repairing cartilage damage. We modified Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG (LGG)-derived BEVs with a chondrocyte-targeting peptide to prolong their therapeutic efficacy. Engineered BEVs, as a drug delivery system, are capable of continuously transporting endogenous miRNAs. Cartilage-targeting LGG-EVs (W-LGG-EVs) penetrate deeply into cartilage tissue and promote extracellular matrix secretion by chondrocytes. Furthermore, W-LGG-EVs were shown to restore cartilage homeostasis and ultimately alleviate stress-related OA. BEVs, as a novel and safe therapeutic agent, hold clinical feasibility.

title: Photo-induced electron pumping meets nanozyme cascade: Triggering multimodal cell death for potent triple-negative breast cancer immunotherapy
abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) treatment is often hindered by tumor hypoxia, cellular survival compensation, and the immuno-suppressive micro-environment. Through the “molecular-electron pumping” strategy, a cyanine photosensitizer BrCy5 with excellent Type I ROS generation ability (two kinds of Type I ROS production of BrCy5 are 308 % and 206 % higher) was developed to realize photodynamic therapy-mediated immunotherapy under tumor hypoxia. In the work, a multifunctional nanoenzyme HMB loaded with Type I photosensitizer was further designed, which precisely delivers BrCy5 and Fe 3+ to tumor cell mitochondria via tumor targeting and lysosomal endocytosis, triggering a lethal cascade of multimodal cell death. Released Fe 3+ catalyzes endogenous H 2 O 2 into O 2 , relieving hypoxia to enhance photodynamic efficacy while depleting glutathione (GSH). Free BrCy5 accumulates in mitochondria, inducing severe mitochondrial dysfunction and lipid peroxidation via efficient ROS generation. This synergistic oxidative stress triggers ferroptosis, activates the Caspase-3/GSDME signaling axis for pyroptosis, leading to massive release of damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) and potent immunogenic cell death (ICD). To enhance this cascade, System Xc - inhibitor sulfasalazine (SSZ) was combined to further deepen GSH depletion and exacerbate ferroptosis. In bilateral tumor-bearing mice, this enhanced regimen created a highly inflamed microenvironment, promoting dendritic cells (DCs) maturation and cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTLs) infiltration, reversing immunosuppression. Ultimately, it inhibited primary and distant tumor growth, converting “cold” to “hot” breast cancer, proposing a transformative strategy for efficient TNBC treatment by combining the “molecular-electron pumping” photosensitizer, multifunctional nanoenzyme carrier, and metabolic pathway blocking to induce multimodal tumor cell death-induced immunotherapy.

title: Coupling photodynamic hypoxia amplification with a self-reporting chemiluminescent prodrug for adaptive precision therapy
abstract: Hypoxia is a hallmark of solid tumors that provides a therapeutic window for hypoxia-activated prodrugs (HAPs). However, the therapeutic performance of HAPs is often limited by heterogeneous tumor hypoxia and the lack of real-time feedback on prodrug activation. Herein, we report a self-reporting nanomedicine, CL-Azo-CPT/Ce6 NPs, that integrates hypoxia amplification with chemiluminescent monitoring in a “Sense-Amplify-Report” strategy. The system combines a photosensitizer, chlorin e6 (Ce6), with a hypoxia-responsive chemiluminescent prodrug, CL-Azo-CPT, in which camptothecin (CPT) is linked to a Schaap's dioxetane scaffold through an azobenzene (azo) trigger. Upon irradiation, Ce6-mediated photodynamic therapy consumes local oxygen and aggravates tumor hypoxia, thereby promoting azoreductase-mediated azo cleavage and accelerating CPT release. This activation process is accompanied by chemiluminescence emission, the intensity of which shows a stoichiometric correlation with drug release and thus provides an excitation-free, real-time readout of prodrug activation. In vitro studies and evaluation in a murine peritoneal metastasis model demonstrated enhanced antitumor efficacy, marked tumor regression, and prolonged survival. This work establishes a hypoxia-amplified and self-reporting chemo-photodynamic platform that addresses two central limitations of HAPs, namely insufficient activation and the absence of in vivo activation feedback.

title: Contractile hydrogel with NIR-induced spatiotemporally programmed release from core-shell nanoparticles for integrated antibacterial and pro-angiogenic healing
abstract: Bacterial colonization, biofilm formation, and microenvironmental dysregulation collectively impede the healing of infected wounds, highlighting the necessity for multifunctional intelligent dressings capable of promoting wound contraction while simultaneously providing antibacterial and regenerative functions. Therefore, this study reported the fabrication of a contractile MPLG hydrogel via the copolymerization of GelMA, NIPAM, and NAGA with Mg@PDA-Lev. Nanoparticle synthesis was performed through Mg 2+ -assisted dopamine polymerization followed by levofloxacin conjugation. The developed platform employs a synergistic therapeutic mechanism in which the acidic wound environment triggers pH-responsive degradation of PDA and subsequent levofloxacin release, while NIR irradiation activates the PDA coating to generate photothermal heat capable of disrupting the bacterial membranes. Furthermore, sustained Mg 2+ release simultaneously facilitated M2 macrophage polarization and stimulated fibroblast activity along with extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling. The thermoresponsive properties of PNIPAM and PNAGA enable the hydrogel to undergo controllable self-contraction upon NIR irradiation while facilitating on-demand drug release. In vitro assays demonstrated the potent broad-spectrum antibacterial activity of MPLG hydrogel against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative pathogens, significantly disrupting biofilms with negligible cytotoxicity. The developed hydrogel integrates synergistic antibacterial, antioxidant, angiogenic, and immunomodulatory effects to restore the wound microenvironment and accelerate healing, representing a promising therapeutic platform for the treatment of infected wounds.

title: Advances in 3D bioprinting of immunoregulatory biomaterials for bone regeneration
abstract: Bone defects caused by trauma, infection, tumour resection, and degenerative diseases remain major clinical challenges because successful regeneration requires coordinated regulation of inflammation, vascularisation, osteogenesis, and bone remodeling. Advances in osteoimmunology have demonstrated that immune responses are integral to each stage of bone healing, shifting biomaterial design from passive biocompatibility towards active and temporally coordinated immunomodulation. Three dimensional bioprinting provides a versatile platform for integrating material, structural, cellular, and biochemical cues within spatially defined constructs, thereby offering new opportunities to regulate the osteoimmune microenvironment. In this review, we first summarise the immune processes and key immune cell populations involved in the inflammatory, proliferative, and remodeling stages of bone repair, and discuss the major bioprinting technologies and bioink design principles relevant to immunoregulatory bone regeneration. We then examine how material composition, structural and surface cues, and biologically active components, including stem cells, cytokines, exosomes, and decellularised extracellular matrix, regulate immune cell states and their interactions with vascular and osteogenic processes. Particular emphasis is placed on moving beyond static macrophage polarisation towards multicellular, stage specific, and spatiotemporally controlled immunoregulation. Finally, current challenges and future directions are discussed, including responsive and multifunctional bioinks, controlled degradation and delivery, mechanistic evaluation, manufacturing standardisation, and clinical translation. Collectively, immunoregulatory bioprinting provides a promising framework for developing bone regenerative constructs that more closely coordinate with the dynamic biology of tissue repair.

title: Activatable MRI nanoprobes for tumor and immune microenvironment imaging: biological mechanisms and translational implications
abstract: Although magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) remains indispensable in oncology, conventional contrast agents lack the biological specificity required to resolve cellular-level pathological events. This review critically examines pivotal advances (2023–2026) in activatable biomaterial-based MRI nanoprobes for precision theranostics. These intelligent platforms convert tumor-associated biological cues into high-fidelity imaging signals while simultaneously enabling targeted therapeutic interventions. We dissect key structural and compositional innovations, spanning high-relaxivity metal-chelating assemblies, zero-background 19 F MRI platforms, and inherently biocompatible, metal-free organic radicals, alongside their controlled activation via microenvironment-responsive, logic-gate architectures. Importantly, we delineate a conceptual shift from tumor-centric imaging toward non-invasive mapping of tumor immune microenvironment dynamics—including macrophage polarization and inflammatory responses—to track immunotherapy efficacy and provide real-time theranostic feedback. Furthermore, we explore how machine learning algorithms serve as a transformative toolkit to accelerate de novo probe design, refine signal quantification, and decipher tumor microenvironment heterogeneity. Finally, to bridge the lab-to-clinic chasm, we benchmark clinical precedents such as AGuIX and ferumoxytol to establish translation-ready design principles for engineering nanoprobes as “imaging drugs” that deliver reproducible, clinically actionable endpoints for precision oncology.

title: Achyranthes bidentata–functionalized bone organoids enhance bone defect repair
abstract: (AB), a traditional osteoactive botanical factor, into a BMSC-derived bone organoid platform to enhance bone regeneration. We first screened AB across a concentration gradient and identified 200 μg/mL as the selected working concentration for promoting BMSC viability, osteogenic differentiation, and matrix mineralization, whereas higher concentrations showed diminished benefit. We then incorporated AB into three-dimensional bone organoid culture to generate AB-bone organoids, which exhibited enhanced viability, increased alkaline phosphatase (ALP) activity and Alizarin Red S (ARS) staining, greater COL-I deposition, and stronger osteogenic marker expression than untreated bone organoids. Functionally, AB-bone organoids outperformed both conventional monolayer BMSCs and untreated organoids, indicating that AB establishes a more potent osteogenic niche within the organoid microenvironment. In a critical-sized calvarial defect model, implantation of AB-bone organoids significantly improved new bone formation, defect bridging, collagen matrix deposition, and osteogenic marker expression compared with untreated organoids or empty defects. As an exploratory clinical extension, we analyzed a retrospective postoperative tibial-fracture cohort and found that systemic oral AB administration was associated with shorter radiographic healing time, higher mRUST scores, lower pain, and better lower-extremity function. Together, this study identifies AB as an organoid-compatible osteoregenerative cue that functionally upgrades bone organoids and supports the translational potential of AB-based organoid engineering for bone repair.

title: An engineered exosome-based platform for targeted delivery to endogenous neural stem cells and fate modulation after spinal cord injury
abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) disrupts neural circuits, leading to persistent sensory and motor deficits. However, effective strategies to promote repair through endogenous neural stem cells (eNSCs) are still limited. In this work, we engineered exosomes with a newly identified peptide (TGP1) to achieve targeted delivery to eNSCs. These exosomes were further loaded with Apelin to stimulate eNSC activation and neuronal differentiation. Following tail-vein administration, TGP1-modified exosomes showed greater accumulation in the injured spinal cord and a 4.6-fold increase in co-localization with Nestin + /SOX2 + eNSC-enriched regions compared with unmodified exosomes. Consequently, the Apln-TGP1 group exhibited a 2.9-fold increase in eNSC proliferation (BrdU + /Nestin + ), a 3.3-fold increase in newborn neurons (BrdU + /DCX + ), and a 4.9-fold increase in BrdU + /NF200 + neuronal-lineage cells compared with the SCI group. Ultimately, the dual-functional treatment was associated with significant improvements in locomotor performance after SCI. Transcriptomic analysis and protein validation indicated that these treatment responses were accompanied by coordinated Apelin-APJ- and PPARγ-related signaling changes. Together, these findings establish a targeted exosomal strategy for modulation of eNSCs and highlight its potential for promoting endogenous repair following SCI.

title: A zinc organic metal skeleton vaccine for lung cancer treatment can stimulate strong innate and adaptive anti-tumor immunity
abstract: Background Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) function as central regulators bridging innate and adaptive immunity in the tumor microenvironment (TME). Therapeutic targeting of TAMs to promote M1 polarization represents a critical strategy for tumor suppression. Methods Herein, we engineered a zinc metal-organic framework functionalized with mannose (MAN) and loaded with CLDN6 antigen (Zn-MAN@CLDN6). We systematically evaluated the anti-tumor efficacy and immunomodulatory functions of Zn-MAN@CLDN6 both in vitro and in vivo . The nanoplatform exhibited the potent cytotoxicity against lung cancer cells and enhanced the macrophage-mediated phagocytosis, while promoting M1 polarization and antigen presentation to activate T cells. Mechanistically, single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) of tumor tissues elucidated the regulatory networks underlying its macrophage-targeted effects. Results The vaccine targeted the highly expressed CD206 receptor on the surface of macrophages through surface modified mannose (MAN), achieving the selective endocytosis. Its acid responsive framework can rapidly degrade under acidic conditions of macrophage lysosomes, releasing Zn 2+ ions and the CLDN6 antigen. The released Zn 2+ acted as an endogenous adjuvant, driving macrophages towards M1 phenotype polarization and enhancing their antigen presentation ability (manifested as upregulation of CD86, MHC-I/II, and IL-12 expression). Meanwhile, macrophages that had undergone the re-education can present CLDN6 antigen to CD8 + T cells through a cross presentation mechanism, effectively activating specific cytotoxic T lymphocytes. In vitro and in vivo experiments had shown that the vaccine can significantly inhibit the growth and metastasis of CLDN6 + lung cancer cells. Research on the mechanism of action had shown that vaccines reshaped the tumor immune microenvironment, effectively recruiting (through CXCR6) and maintaining the survival and expansion of infiltrating CD8 + T cells by upregulating macrophages expression of CXCL16 and IL-15 through regulating the JAK3/STAT5 signal pathway. In addition, the vaccine demonstrated synergistic anti-tumor effects when combined with PD-1 immune checkpoint blockade therapy. The biosafety assessment showed that it had good biocompatibility. Conclusion This study developed a nano vaccine platform that integrated targeted delivery, immune regulation, and specific anti-tumor response, providing a new strategy for immunotherapy of CLDN6 + lung cancer.

title: A bottleneck-first evaluation of antigen delivery platforms for therapeutic cancer vaccines
abstract: Therapeutic cancer vaccines require tumor-relevant antigens and delivery systems that preserve antigen integrity, control tissue and cellular exposure, support productive processing, and sustain antigen-specific immunity. Yet platform performance cannot be inferred from material properties, cellular uptake, or tumor control alone, because these endpoints do not identify which delivery step changed or whether that change contributed to an antigen-specific response. Seven material matrices and a separate carrier-free molecular assembly mode are evaluated across four functional domains. A carrier advantage is supported only when a defined variable changes a prespecified delivery function under matched conditions, a matched delivery endpoint captures that change, and the result is linked to an antigen-specific outcome; selected variable-to-outcome chains are appraised qualitatively using four possible categories: supported, partial, untested, or refuted. Repeat-dose behavior, carrier-directed immunity, routine lot release, manufacturing consistency, and comparability following manufacturing process changes are treated as additional constraints because they can modify or confound an initial advantage. Artificial intelligence-assisted design is considered only for hypothesis triage and validation planning. The reviewed evidence does not support a universal platform hierarchy. Platform selection should instead begin with the dominant biological or product-level bottleneck.

title: Corrigendum to “Polygonatum sibiricum polysaccharide-based hydrogels regulate macrophage mitochondrial homeostasis for the treatment of radiodermatitis” [Mater. Today Bio 40 (2026) 103520]
Cancer-cell-mimicking MnO2 nanoplatform delivers immunological adjuvants to enhance radio-immunotherapy
abstract: The hypoxic and immunosuppressive microenvironment within tumors represents a fundamental mechanism contributing to radiotherapy (RT) resistance, which is closely linked to poor prognosis in cancer patients. To overcome these limitations, we constructed a tumor cell membrane-mimetic manganese-based nanoplatform for delivering immune adjuvants (MnO 2 -R848@CM) to synergistically enhance the efficacy of clinical radiotherapy. In vitro experiments demonstrated that MnO 2 -R848@CM is rapidly and specifically taken up by 4T1 cells. Upon X-ray irradiation, immunogenic cell death (ICD) and released Mn 2+ activated the cGAS-STING pathway in dendritic cells (DCs), synergistically accelerating DCs maturation alongside R848 to trigger downstream immune response cascades. In breast cancer mouse models, MnO 2 –R848@CM exhibited highly effective homotargeting properties, rapidly accumulating and persisting at tumor sites. It further established a long-lasting adaptive anti-tumor immune response via multiple pathways, effectively accelerating tumor ablation and significantly inhibiting tumor growth in tumor-bearing mice. These findings highlight the potential of the MnO 2 –R848@CM nanoplatform in advancing synergistic cancer radioimmunotherapy, which effectively integrates the direct cytotoxic effects of radiotherapy with ongoing antitumor immune responses.

title: In situ delivery of cannabidiol-loaded GelMA sponge attenuates cerebral edema and neuroinflammation in traumatic brain injury
abstract: BackgroundTraumatic brain injury (TBI) is a critical neurological condition, in which secondary injury is amplified by a tightly coupled cascade of cerebral edema and neuroinflammatory responses. Although cannabidiol (CBD) exhibits neuroprotective and anti-inflammatory activity in experimental TBI, therapeutic translation remains limited by inefficient delivery and insufficient accumulation at injury sites. This study developed a gelatin methacryloyl-based CBD-loaded sponge (GM-CBD) for in situ, sustained release to enhance local therapeutic efficacy.MethodsMaterial properties and CBD incorporation were characterized using Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, nuclear magnetic resonance, and scanning electron microscopy. Degradation kinetics, swelling behavior, and biocompatibility were comprehensively assessed in vitro and in vivo. Liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry quantified CBD distribution in injured brain tissue. A rat model of TBI was generated via application of the Feeney free-fall impact approach, and therapeutic efficacy was assessed alongside transcriptome-based mechanistic investigation.ResultsGM-CBD exhibited a porous architecture with lesion-adaptive swelling, sustained drug release, biodegradability, and excellent biosafety. Local CBD accumulation in the injured cortex increased significantly. Treatment improved neurological outcomes by promoting M2-type microglial polarization, suppressing astrocytic reactivity, restoring endothelial and blood-brain barrier integrity, and reducing aquaporin-4 expression. These changes stabilized the neurovascular unit and disrupted the edema-inflammation cycle. RNA sequencing revealed that anti-inflammatory signaling and restoration of cerebral microenvironmental homeostasis mediated the observed neuroprotection.ConclusionsThe GM-CBD platform provides a localized, sustained-release strategy that enhances CBD efficacy in acute TBI and represents a translational therapeutic approach for neurotrauma and other inflammatory brain disorders.

title: Hyaluronic acid-based osmolality-responsive immediate-release microneedles co-loading baicalein and astaxanthin for oral ulcer therapy
abstract: Oral ulcers, a prevalent mucosal disorder, are clinically managed by topical corticosteroids and immunosuppressants to alleviate symptoms. However, conventional therapies suffer from suboptimal drug bioavailability, inconsistent efficacy, and potential adverse effects. To address these limitations, using natural carbohydrate polymer hyaluronic acid (HA) with excellent biocompatibility, as the main substrate, we constructed the osmolality-responsive immediate-release microneedles (MNs) platform (GA@BA&Ast MNs) co-loading baicalein (BA) and astaxanthin (Ast) for oral ulcer therapy, which effectively addresses traditional treatment bottlenecks via responsive immediate-release and efficient absorption. The platform's core innovation lies in its dynamically controllable release mechanism, which is triggered specifically by the oral microenvironment. Its osmolality-responsive mechanism, relying on HA-Ca 2+ dynamic coordination network dissociation in oral fluid, enables rapid disintegration and delivery speed superior to conventional microneedles, with good mechanical strength for irritation-free mucosal penetration and 85.3%/87.1% cumulative BA/Ast release within 20 minutes. In the rat model, GA@BA&Ast MNs significantly accelerated ulcer healing, increased collagen deposition and VEGF expression by 41.22% and 47.05%, and exerted complementary antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, and ROS scavenging effects by promoting epithelial migration and angiogenesis. This responsive MNs platform overcomes the limitations of hydrophobic drug delivery, providing a promising universal strategy for localized orofacial diseases, such as oral ulcers, oral fibrosis, and oral cancer.

title: A cell-adaptive nanostructured hydrogel enables an early regenerative microenvironment for peripheral nerve repair
abstract: Nerve conduits serve as critical clinical tools for peripheral nerve repair, yet delayed intraluminal endogenous cellular occupation significantly impedes early nerve regeneration. Cell-adaptive fillers capable of dynamically supporting endogenous cellular activities would provide an early regenerative microenvironment to accelerate nerve repair. Here, we show a cell-adaptive nanostructured hydrogel-filled nerve conduit for improving peripheral nerve repair. This hydrogel is formed by gelatin methacryloyl via self-assembly and photopolymerization-based printing. It features a unique nanostructure that could fast adapt cells via squeeze-induced space release. Meanwhile, this nanostructured hydrogel can promote Schwann cell proliferation and migration, and cellular contact formation, which may be associated with enhanced cell-matrix interactions and mechanotransduction-related responses. Filling into a conduit composed of inner electrospun fiber layer and outer hydrogel layer, this hydrogel significantly facilitates Schwann cell occupation compared to hollow conduits at one-week post-implantation. A 10 mm nerve defect is reconnected by regenerative nerve bridges in the hydrogel-filled conduit accompanied by substantial hydrogel degradation within 24 days. At 12 weeks post-surgery, this conduit treatment induces better nerve regeneration and functional recovery than the conventional conduit treatment. This work demonstrates a nanostructured cell-adaptive hydrogel for engineering early regenerative microenvironments, providing a promising biomaterial platform for peripheral nerve repair.

title: ZIF-8-gated cascade nanoreactor amplifies glucose-triggered CO release and ferroptosis for mild photothermal cancer therapy
abstract: Mild photothermal therapy offers a safer alternative to conventional hyperthermia, but its therapeutic efficacy is frequently compromised by heat-shock protection, metabolic compensation and insufficient intracellular oxidative damage. Herein, we developed a ZIF-8-gated cascade nanoreactor, denoted ZIF/HMPB-CO@GOx, to amplify glucose-triggered carbon monoxide release and ferroptosis for enhanced mild photothermal cancer therapy. In this system, hollow mesoporous photothermal nanocores were loaded with a CO donor and glucose oxidase, followed by ZIF-8 coating as an acid-responsive gatekeeper. The ZIF-8 shell protected the catalytic payloads under physiological conditions and promoted intracellular release in the acidic tumor microenvironment. Upon 808 nm laser irradiation, the nanoreactor generated mild hyperthermia and accelerated cascade reactions, in which GOx catalyzed glucose oxidation to produce H₂O₂, subsequently triggering CO release and reactive oxygen species generation. This glucose-amplified CO generation simultaneously suppressed glycolysis and mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation, leading to ATP depletion, lactate reduction and downregulation of HSP70. Meanwhile, metal-mediated redox cycling, glutathione consumption and GPX4 inhibition intensified lipid peroxidation and ferroptotic cell death, as further supported by ferroptosis-rescue and transcriptomic analyses. In 4T1 tumor-bearing mice, ZIF/HMPB-CO@GOx enabled enhanced tumor accumulation, efficient mild photothermal heating and pronounced tumor growth suppression with negligible body-weight loss. This ZIF-8-gated nanoreactor establishes a glucose-powered gas-releasing strategy to overcome thermal resistance and potentiate ferroptosis-mediated cancer therapy.

title: AT-RvD1 liposomes effectively accumulate in spinal cord and reprogram microglia via ANGPTL4-SUCLG1-propionate axis for treating neuropathic pain
abstract: Neuropathic pain (NP) remains a major clinical challenge as current medications are ineffective in treating the underlying cause, and the clinical use of these drugs also has adverse reactions such as addiction. Therefore, specialized pro-resolving mediators (SPMs) may represent a promising therapeutic strategy. Microglia-mediated neuroinflammation is central to NP pathogenesis, yet feasible strategies for precise modulation of microglial inflammatory responses remain limited. Here, we reveal that aspirin-triggered resolvin D1 (AT-RvD1) promotes a shift of microglia toward an anti-inflammatory and pro-repair state via a novel ANGPTL4-SUCLG1-propionate axis, consequently attenuating neuroinflammation and pain hypersensitivity in mice models with NP. To address invasive nature of intrathecal injection limitation in NP clinical treatment, an MG1 peptide-modified liposomal delivery system encapsulating AT-RvD1 (AT-RvD1@Lipo-MG1) is developed. Intravenous administration of this nanoplatform enables effective and targeted delivery of AT-RvD1 to spinal microglia, with robust analgesic and anti-inflammatory effects and favorable biosafety in vivo. This study elucidates a novel mechanism through which AT-RvD1 modulates microglial inflammatory responses and proposes a highly translatable nanotherapeutic strategy for the treatment of NP.

title: Graphene oxide-induced multiple iPSC spheroid formation for enhanced production of angiogenic exosomes accelerating tissue regeneration
abstract: Exosome-based therapeutics have emerged as a promising cell-free strategy for tissue regeneration by coordinating angiogenesis and tissue repair. Induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived exosomes are particularly attractive because of their regenerative potential and scalability; however, the reproducible and scalable production of functionally potent exosomes remains a major barrier to clinical translation. Here, we developed a graphene oxide (GO)-mediated nanoengineering strategy to establish a multi-spheroid platform that simultaneously regulates spheroid architecture, enhances exosome production, and improves angiogenic functionality in both iPSC spheroids and iPSC-derived vascular endothelial cell (vEC) spheroids. GO reproducibly reorganized cellular aggregation from a single dominant spheroid into multiple uniformly sized spheroids per well and increased exosome production while preserving characteristic vesicle properties. GO-engineered iPSC spheroid-derived exosomes exhibited distinct angiogenesis-related miRNA profiles and significantly enhanced endothelial cell migration and capillary-like network formation in vitro. Extending this strategy to iPSC-vEC spheroids further enhanced endothelial differentiation and generated lineage-specific exosomes with greater pro-angiogenic activity. In a rat full-thickness skin wound model, GO-engineered spheroid-derived exosomes accelerated wound closure and promoted vascularized skin regeneration. Collectively, these findings establish GO-mediated spheroid nanoengineering as a reproducible and potentially scalable strategy for producing therapeutically potent exosomes. By integrating controlled spheroid formation, enhanced exosome productivity, preserved vesicle characteristics, and improved angiogenic efficacy, this platform provides a practical framework for standardized exosome manufacturing and supports its future clinical translation toward vascular regenerative therapies.

title: NIR-responsive carbon monoxide nanoplatform for synergistic antibacterial and anti-inflammatory therapy of refractory keratitis and biofilm-infected wounds
abstract: Drug-resistant bacterial biofilms hinder the treatment of persistent infections by limiting drug penetration and reducing bacterial susceptibility through their dense extracellular matrix and active signaling networks. Herein, we developed a near-infrared (NIR) light-responsive, bacteria-targeting nanoplatform, termed UCMSP-CL, for localized carbon monoxide (CO) delivery and biofilm eradication. UCMSP-CL disrupts biofilm architecture and adheres to bacteria through electrostatic interactions and enzyme-substrate recognition. Subsequent NIR irradiation triggers local CO release, which induces severe bacterial metabolic exhaustion by inhibiting the bacterial respiratory chain, depleting ATP and compromising membrane integrity, while exerting potent anti-inflammatory effects. In murine models of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) keratitis and infected skin wounds, NIR-irradiated UCMSP-CL markedly reduced bacterial burden, promoted biofilm clearance, alleviated local inflammation, and accelerated tissue repair. These findings establish a controllable platform that couples antibacterial and anti-inflammatory activities, offering a potential strategy for treating biofilm-associated and drug-resistant infections.

title: 660 nm LED preconditioning programs mitochondrial signaling in BMSCs for functional tracheal cartilage regeneration
abstract: Stem-cell-based cartilage regeneration is limited not only by cell delivery, but also by the difficulty of establishing a stable and functionally competent regenerative cell state before implantation. Here, we report a photonic mitochondrial programming strategy in which 660 nm light-emitting diode (LED) irradiation preconditions bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) to enhance functional tracheal cartilage regeneration. BMSCs were seeded onto egg white-derived ring-shaped porous scaffolds and exposed to defined 660 nm LED irradiation before implantation. Among the tested irradiation conditions, 15 J/cm 2 optimally promoted BMSC proliferation, chondrogenic differentiation and cartilage-like extracellular matrix deposition, while suppressing fibrotic, hypertrophic and matrix-degrading phenotypes. Mechanistically, 660 nm LED irradiation enhanced cytochrome c oxidase (CCO) activity, mitochondrial membrane potential, adenosine triphosphate (ATP) production and respiratory function, accompanied by moderate reactive oxygen species (ROS) signaling. This mitochondrial bioenergetic–redox response activated the PI3K/Akt/mTOR/GSK3β–SOX9 axis, thereby promoting type II collagen, aggrecan and glycosaminoglycan-rich matrix formation. Pharmacological inhibition of ROS signaling, mitochondrial activity, PI3K or mTOR attenuated the LED-induced chondrogenic program. In a rabbit tracheal cartilage ring defect model, 15 J/cm 2 -preconditioned BMSC–scaffold constructs improved cartilage-like tissue formation, airway epithelial repair, lumen patency and mechanical support after 30 days of observation. These findings support 660 nm LED irradiation as a controllable mitochondrial preconditioning strategy for stem-cell-based functional cartilage regeneration.

title: An artificial intelligence-assisted PARP-1-targeted PET imaging agent [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-FZPF: From bench to clinic
abstract: Considering that clinical data of 68 Ga-labeled poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP)-targeted probes have not yet been reported, and integrated artificial intelligence (AI) workflows for radiotracer development are still lacking. To support radiotracer development and clinical translation, we constructed an AI-assisted multi-stage prioritization workflow and then synthesized two 68 Ga-labeled PARP-1-targeted probes, validating their performance through in vitro , in vivo , and clinical evaluations. An AI-guided multi-objective workflow (encoder-decoder recurrent neural network (RNN) generation, convolutional neural network (CNN) docking scoring, Synthetic Complexity Learned from a Reaction Corpus (SCScore)-based tractability triage, and deep neural network (DNN)) was used to prioritize a derivatization-ready Fuzuloparib analog (NH 2 -FZPF) and to guide chelator installation, yielding DOTA-FZPF and NOTA-FZPF precursors for subsequent 68 Ga radiolabeling. Both [ 68 Ga]Ga-DOTA-FZPF and [ 68 Ga]Ga-NOTA-FZPF exhibited high radiochemical purity, stability, and PARP-1-targeted specificity. In tumor models, [ 68 Ga]Ga-DOTA-FZPF displayed favorable tumor uptake and rapid background clearance, supporting further evaluation. Exploratory positron emission tomography (PET) assessments of Fuzuloparib target engagement show the specificity and functionality of [ 68 Ga]Ga-DOTA-FZPF, supporting in vivo evaluation of PARP inhibitor target engagement and pharmacodynamics. This study recruited 4 cancer patients and performed positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) scans using [ 68 Ga]Ga-DOTA-FZPF. Biopsy specimens showed that PET/CT-positive lesions corresponded to regions of high PARP-1 expression. This study demonstrates how an AI rational design workflow can support decision-making in radiotracer design while maintaining synthetic feasibility and translational potential. These preliminary findings support the clinical feasibility of [ 68 Ga]Ga-DOTA-FZPF and suggest that it is promising for non-invasive assessment of PARP-1 expression and dynamic monitoring of in vivo target occupancy and pharmacodynamics.

title: An intrascrotal bioadhesive nanoplatform for sustained hydrogen delivery ameliorates age-associated testicular dysfunction
abstract: Testicular aging is characterized by progressive spermatogenic decline. Accumulating oxidative injury and insufficient metabolic support from Sertoli cells may contribute to this process. Although molecular hydrogen has shown antioxidant potential, its therapeutic application in reproductive aging is limited by rapid dissipation after administration. To overcome this barrier, we developed the localized hydrogen-releasing system S-H/B. This platform integrates hydrogenated silicon nanosheets (S-H) with a bioadhesive polymer, aldehyde-functionalized polylactic acid-hyperbranched polyglycerol (PLA-HPG-al). The resulting formulation adhered to peritesticular tissue following intrascrotal injection, showed prolonged local retention, and enabled sustained hydrogen release under physiological conditions. This sustained local hydrogen delivery reduced age-associated testicular degeneration and promoted spermatogenesis in aged mice. Notably, single-cell RNA sequencing revealed enhanced HIF-1 signaling and glycolysis-related transcriptional programs in aged Sertoli cells following S-H/B treatment. Further mechanistic analyses indicated that S-H/B reduced ONOO − levels and limited PHD1-dependent HIF-1α hydroxylation, thereby slowing HIF-1α degradation and promoting its nuclear localization. Consistently, S-H/B increased glycolytic enzyme expression, glucose uptake, glycolytic flux, and lactate production in Sertoli cells, whereas HIF-1α inhibition attenuated these metabolic changes. The increased lactate production may have contributed to improved seminiferous epithelial function. Overall, this work presents a bioadhesive hydrogen delivery strategy for age-associated male reproductive dysfunction and suggests that metabolic remodeling in Sertoli cells may contribute to its beneficial effects.

title: Coordination-strengthened Rhein/Pectin@Zn dual-network hydrogel for local antitumor therapy
abstract: Local therapeutic platforms capable of concurrent tumor-cell elimination and antiangiogenic activity are urgently needed. This study presents a Rhein/Pectin@Zn hydrogel fabricated through supramolecular self-assembly and metal-coordination crosslinking and administered by dual-syringe in situ gelation. Hydrogels prepared under standardized ex vivo crosslinking conditions display a porous microstructure, stable gel characteristics, shear-dependent flow behavior, and accelerated cargo release under acidic conditions. Biological evaluations indicate antiproliferative and pro-apoptotic effects against tumor cells, together with reduced endothelial angiogenic signaling. Repeated intratumoral delivery in a subcutaneous B16 melanoma model reduced endpoint tumor volume and weight without overt major-organ histopathological abnormalities in the displayed fields. Integrated transcriptomic and molecular analyses implicated cell-cycle checkpoint disruption and apoptosis-associated signaling in the observed antitumor response. Collectively, this work positions Rhein/Pectin@Zn as an in situ-forming hydrogel for local cancer therapy.

title: Engineering immune cell engagers: From molecular constructs to biomaterial platforms
abstract: Immune cell engagers (ICEs) are emerging therapeutic platforms that redirect immune effector cells toward cancer cells by physically bridging immune-cell receptors with tumor-associated targets. This cell-bridging mechanism converts molecular recognition into localized immune activation, immune synapse formation, cytotoxic killing, or phagocytic clearance. Such contact-centered immune redirection complements immune checkpoint blockade, which can restore antitumor immunity but does not directly promote the physical immune cell-tumor cell contact required for productive effector functions. Building on this principle, advances in molecular and biomaterial engineering have expanded ICE design beyond conventional molecular formats, enabling programmable molecular bridges, engineered living cell surfaces, and material-scaffolded systems that coordinate tumor targeting, immune-cell recruitment, and functional modulation. In this review, we organized these approaches according to three levels of ICE engineering: (1) molecular ICEs such as engineered antibodies and aptamers, (2) living cell engagers based on cell surface engineering using molecular constructs or biomaterials and (3) nanoparticle platforms. Across these platforms, we discuss molecular architecture, tumor-targeting specificity, immune cell recruitment, and functional modulation as key factors governing direct immune-tumor cell interactions. By connecting diverse strategies through a common cell-engagement perspective, this review highlights how these approaches can provide functional and spatial advantages for next-generation cancer immunotherapy.

title: A CNS-targeted atovaquone nanotherapy mitigates complement activation and neuromuscular degeneration in ALS
abstract: Complement-mediated glial inflammation and synaptic injury are increasingly implicated in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), but clinically translatable complement-modulating therapies remain limited. Atovaquone (ATQ) is an approved, poorly water-soluble small molecule with reported immunomodulatory activity. We investigated whether ATQ could modulate C1qb or C5aR1-associated pathology and whether lactoferrin (Lf)-derived nanomicelles could improve delivery to the spinal cord. ALS spinal-cord single-cell transcriptomic and pathway-enrichment analyses were combined with screening of an FDA-approved drug library, molecular docking and surface plasmon resonance (SPR). Lf-ATQ nanomicelles were characterised by dynamic light scattering, transmission electron microscopy and fluorescence distribution studies. Complement/inflammasome responses were examined in microglial and motor-neuron–microglia models. Therapeutic effects were evaluated in mice expressing the human superoxide dismutase 1 G93A variant (SOD1 G93A ) by motor testing, compound muscle action potential recording, histology, immunostaining, western blotting and proteomics. Complement genes, particularly C1qb and C5aR1, were enriched in microglia, whereas glutamatergic-synapse and axon-guidance programmes were negatively enriched. In cellular models and SOD1 G93A spinal cord, Lf-ATQ reduced C1qb, NLRP3 and multiple inflammatory mediators, attenuated glial reactivity and altered autophagy-related proteins. Treatment preserved rotarod performance, grip strength, gait parameters, compound muscle action potential amplitude and gastrocnemius morphology. Proteomic analysis indicated remodelling of complement/coagulation, vesicular-transport and synaptic modules. These findings support Lf-ATQ as a central nervous system (CNS) -oriented, complement-regulating nanotherapy candidate for ALS. Direct functional target-inhibition assays, quantitative ATQ pharmacokinetics, long-term safety assessment and validation in non-SOD1 models remain necessary before translational conclusions can be drawn.

title: Conductive hydrogel bioelectronics for chronic neuromodulation: From biomimetic design and bioactive interfaces to integrated neural platforms
abstract: In biomedical engineering, hydrogel bioelectronics brings together the interface between flexible electronic devices and biological systems, opening up a new way for chronic neural regulation. Here we focus on the recent progress in this field, from material design to system integration. The design of high-performance conductive hydrogels is an entry point. The multi-level structure engineering strategy, such as the introduction of carbon nanotubes or conductive polymers, can raise the conductivity and mechanical toughness together. When biomimetic adhesion molecules such as polydopamine or tannic acid are added, the hydrogel has the ability of wet tissue adhesion, and anti swelling and active anti-inflammatory functions are also embedded in the material system. As a result, the resulting neural interfaces are not only more durable in practical applications but also ensure excellent biocompatibility. Turning to applications. How does this kind of material promote the development of chronic neuromodulation technology? Peripheral nerve repair, brain computer interface, spinal cord injury, autonomic nervous system regulation can be seen in several scenes. The long-term and high-precision recording and regulation of neural signals is exactly the most important link in these applications. Hydrogel electronics does have its own uniqueness in this regard. However, there is still a long way to go between laboratory research and clinical transformation. How to ensure long-term stability? Can controllable degradation be achieved in practice? Will the signal fidelity drop with time? How to optimize wireless operation and system integration? Large scale manufacturing is an unavoidable reality test. These directions are probably the worthy areas for follow-up research. Looking forward, if the lines of intelligent response materials, closed-loop sensing and control, and advanced micro processing technology can be screwed together, hydrogel bioelectronics may truly move towards the next generation of personalized, dynamic and adaptive neural diagnosis and treatment platform.

title: Piezoelectric ZnO-incorporated bioactive glass nanospheres for enhanced odontogenic differentiation and angiogenesis
abstract: Regeneration of the pulp–dentin complex requires coordinated odontogenic differentiation and vascularization, which remain difficult to achieve using conventional biomaterials that rely predominantly on biochemical stimulation. Herein, we developed an ultrasound-responsive nanocomposite system composed of ZnO-incorporated mesoporous bioactive glass nanospheres (Z-MBGNs) to introduce an externally controllable electromechanical cue alongside material-derived ionic signals. By incorporating ZnO-containing phases into the mesoporous bioactive glass matrix, the composite enabled sustained release of Zn 2+ and Ca 2+ while reducing the cytotoxicity associated with excessive ZnO-derived ion exposure. Under LIPUS stimulation, Z-MBGNs exhibited an ultrasound-associated electromechanical/electrical response and further enhanced odontogenic and angiogenic responses. In vitro, LIPUS-treated 10Z-MBGNs increased hDPSC migration, ALP activity, mineralized matrix formation, and DSPP/DMP-1 expression, while also enhancing HUVEC tube formation and angiogenesis-related factor expression. In a subcutaneous ectopic implantation model, the treatment promoted extracellular matrix deposition and increased odontogenic- and angiogenic-associated marker expression. Collectively, these findings provide proof-of-concept evidence that Z-MBGNs can combine sustained ionic regulation with ultrasound-associated electromechanical responsiveness to enhance coordinated odontogenic and angiogenic behaviors. Further studies incorporating appropriate mechanistic controls and tooth-specific orthotopic models are required to clarify the underlying mechanisms and translational potential of this strategy.

title: Injectable self-healing polysaccharide hydrogel with slow-release b-FGF for adipose tissue regeneration
abstract: Soft tissue defects require the application of adipose tissue reconstruction techniques; however, these approaches often face challenges such as low survival rates due to mechanical pressure and inadequate blood supply. This study presents the development of an injectable, self-healing polysaccharide hydrogel designed for the slow release of basic fibroblast growth factor (b-FGF) that utilizes oxidized hyaluronic acid (OHA) and carbohydrazide-modified gelatin (Gel-CDH) as foundational components. The hydrogel is characterized by an optimal pore size, porosity, mechanical properties, and degradation behavior, in addition to excellent biocompatibility, all of which facilitate adipose tissue growth. In vitro experiments revealed that the OHA/Gel-CDH polysaccharide hydrogel significantly enhanced the adipogenic differentiation of adipose-derived stem cells. Furthermore, the implantation of the polysaccharide hydrogel in conjunction with an autologous fat graft suspension into the subcutaneous of the rat dorsal region resulted in improved adipose tissue survival and the regeneration of vascularized adipose tissue. These results suggest that the use of an injectable, self-healing OHA/Gel-CDH polysaccharide hydrogel with slow-released b-FGF in combination with autologous fat grafting is a promising strategy for the repair of soft tissue defects.

title: Self-powered bioelectronics for peripheral nerve regeneration: Electroactive materials, energy transduction, and therapeutic mechanisms
abstract: Peripheral nerve injuries remain difficult to treat because axonal regeneration is slow, incomplete, and highly dependent on timely biochemical, structural, and electrical cues. Self-powered electroceuticals offer an emerging route to deliver localized electrical stimulation with reduced dependence on bulky batteries and percutaneous leads. This review summarizes recent advances in self-powered bioelectronic systems for nerve repair, with emphasis on three representative platforms: self-electrified galvanic devices, triboelectric nanogenerators, and piezoelectric nanogenerators. From a materials and interfacial engineering perspective, we discuss how redox reactions, contact electrification, and piezoelectric polarization convert physiological or externally applied energy into therapeutic electrical outputs. Key design factors, including biodegradable metals, electroactive polymers, piezoelectric composites, conductive interfaces, encapsulation strategies, and nerve-guidance architectures, are critically examined in relation to output stability, degradation behavior, tissue compatibility, and regenerative efficacy. We further highlight preclinical evidence that self-powered electrical cues influence Schwann cell activity, axonal elongation, neurotrophic factor secretion, immune modulation, and downstream signaling pathways to enhance myelination, suppress muscle atrophy, and improve functional recovery. Finally, current limitations and future opportunities are discussed, including stimulation-dose standardization, degradation-byproduct management, scalable fabrication, closed-loop integration, and large-animal validation. This review provides a unified-materials-interface-device-biology framework for developing clinically translatable self-powered electroceuticals for nerve regeneration.

title: Localized nanomedicine for urologic cancers: anatomy-guided design and clinical translation
abstract: Bladder, prostate, and renal cancers differ in their anatomical locations, tissue structures, and routes of clinical intervention. Conventional systemic treatments are often limited by nonspecific biodistribution, insufficient tumor accumulation, and toxicity. Localized nanomedicine delivery offers an alternative strategy by using organ-specific anatomical access to increase exposure at the tumor site and reduce systemic distribution. Its success depends on the compatibility of nanomedicine delivery systems with the physiological environment, anatomical characteristics, and procedural requirements of the organ. Here, we compare local nanomedicine strategies for these three cancers and discuss how anatomy can guide their design. We therefore define five design criteria for localized nanomedicines: retention, penetration, responsiveness, targeting, and synergy. For each criterion, describe relevant engineering approaches and applications in individual cancers. We also consider barriers to clinical use, including formulation reproducibility and compatibility with clinical workflows. An approach that combines anatomy, nanomedicine design, and delivery procedures may support their clinical translation for more precise diagnosis and treatment.

title: Microenvironment-responsive injectable marine polysaccharide hydrogel empowered by bimetallic MOF nanozymes for in situ pancreatic cancer immunotherapy via ferroptosis-mediated cGAS-STING activation
abstract: Pancreatic cancer is characterized by a dense desmoplastic stroma and a profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME), which jointly impede drug penetration and immune activation. Here, we report a microenvironment-responsive injectable marine polysaccharide hydrogel (G@ZnFe-Gel) empowered by a Zn/Fe bimetallic MOF nanozyme to achieve in situ pancreatic cancer immunotherapy via ferroptosis-cGAS-STING synergy. Following intratumoral injection, the hydrogel undergoes rapid thermally and Ca 2+ -reinforced gelation, forming a stable intratumoral depot that ensures prolonged local retention within stromal-dense pancreatic tumors. Mechanistically, glucose oxidase (GOD)-mediated glucose oxidation disrupts tumor metabolism while generating H 2 O 2 , which is further converted into highly reactive oxygen species through Fe 3+ -mediated Fenton-like reactions, inducing lipid peroxidation and ferroptosis. Comparisons with the Zn-Gel control further support the additional contributions of Fe incorporation and GOD loading to the enhanced ferroptosis-associated responses. In addition, ferroptosis-associated mitochondrial stress and potential DAMP release, including mtDNA, may contribute to enhanced cGAS-STING signaling, with a possible additional contribution from Zn 2+ signaling. In a subcutaneous pancreatic cancer model, G@ZnFe-Gel markedly suppressed tumor growth, promotes macrophage reprogramming, enhanced cytotoxic T-cell infiltration, and remodeled the immunosuppressive TME without systemic toxicity. This work establishes a mechanism-driven hydrogel-nanozyme platform that integrates local retention, regulated cell death, and innate-adaptive immune crosstalk, offering a promising strategy for immunologically cold and stroma-rich solid tumors.

title: Chirality and morphology-dependent siRNA delivery for targeted lung cancer therapy with intrinsically chiral gold nanoparticles
abstract: The clinical translation of RNA interference (RNAi) for lung cancer treatment remains hampered by the lack of delivery vectors that concurrently optimize cellular uptake, target specificity, and in vivo stability. This work reports an intrinsically chiral gold nanoparticle (Au NP) platform with precisely controlled morphology for targeted siRNA delivery. Through a full 2 × 2 factorial design (2 chiralities × 2 morphologies), the work decouples the individual and combined contributions of these two parameters. It is found that right-handed chiral nanoparticles (D-NPs) show significantly faster cellular internalization and higher gene silencing potency than left-handed (L-NPs) and achiral (DL-NPs) counterparts. Beyond chirality, nanoparticle morphology serves as an equally critical parameter: the rhombicuboctahedral (RCO) architecture yields markedly higher silencing efficacy than cubic counterparts with D-chirality. Furthermore, proteomic analysis revealed that Au RCO nanoparticles with different chirality displayed distinct functional enrichment profiles. By D-RCO combination with minimal surface modification, siRNA targeting PD-L1 achieves potent knockdown and robust inhibition of H460 lung cancer proliferation both in vitro and in vivo. This work establishes chirality and morphology as co-designable parameters for gene delivery and provides a mechanistic blueprint for translating chiral nanomaterials into solid tumor therapy.

title: Tumor microenvironment-responsive manganese nanocarriers for on-demand release of methotrexate and DNAzyme in MiR-155-driven cervical cancer
abstract: Cervical cancer is a prevalent form of cancer that affects women on a global scale. MicroRNA-155 (miR-155) has been identified as a key player in cervical cancer, with its over-expression signifying a promising target for therapeutic interventions. However, the molecular mechanisms by which miR-155 contributes to the invasive progression of cervical cancer, as well as miRNA-based therapeutic approaches, remain to be elucidated. To address the issues, we initially investigated the functional role of miR-155 in cervical cancer progression. In vitro and in vivo results demonstrated that miR-155 was closely associated with the malignant progression of cervical cancer through regulation of the epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) process, specifically by directly targeting ZFPM2 protein, thereby exerting oncogenic effects. Based on these findings, we designed manganese-based composite agents, namely MnO 2 @PDA-DNAzyme-substrate-methotrexate nanoparticles (MPDM NPs), for simultaneous miRNA imaging and chemotherapy toward cervical cancer. The MPDM NPs exhibited favorable biocompatibility and tumor microenvironment (TME) responsive release behavior, allowing controlled release of Mn 2+ , methotrexate (MTX), and DNAzyme probes for miR-155 detection and therapeutic intervention. In vivo studies with tumor-bearing mice indicated that the MPDM NPs could effectively target tumors. The Mn 2+ -activate miRNA imaging achieved a detection limit for miR-155 of 0.3 nM. Moreover, the drug MTX enabled tumor chemotherapy by regulating the EMT process. This, in turn, has resulted in an impressive tumor inhibition rate of 86.2%. This proposed strategy indicated significant potential for the advancement of precision theranostics in the context of cervical cancer.

title: AICAR-induced energy supply and paracrine activity of endothelial cells accelerate chronic diabetic wound healing by promoting angiogenesis and modulating macrophage reprogramming
abstract: Chronic diabetic wound healing is severely hampered by endothelial cell (EC) dysfunction, defective angiogenesis, and a persistent inflammatory microenvironment, yet the crosstalk between EC energy metabolism and macrophage polarization in this process remains poorly understood. Here, we identified an AMPK-dependent metabolic pathway in ECs that orchestrated both angiogenic restoration and macrophage immune reprogramming for diabetic wound repair, and translated this mechanism into a functional three-dimensional (3D) scaffold (MEWs+GelMA@AI) fabricated by melt electrospinning writing technology. Acadesine (AICAR) efficiently induced a high-energy state in ECs by activating AMPK, preserving mitochondrial ultrastructure, enhancing respiratory-chain complex activity, and increasing VEGF expression and angiogenic potential. Notably, we discovered that AI-EXO, secreted by these metabolically activated ECs, delivered GAS6 to macrophages as a key paracrine factor, thereby triggering activation of the MER/AKT pathway and driving M1-to-M2 polarization. To our knowledge, this is the first report identifying exosomal GAS6 as a mediator of EC-macrophage crosstalk in diabetic wound healing. The MEWs+GelMA@AI scaffold, characterized by a porous structure and sustained AICAR release, exhibited excellent cytocompatibility and proangiogenic activity in vitro . In vivo , the scaffold significantly accelerated diabetic wound closure by promoting neovascularization, reducing inflammatory infiltration, and increasing the M2/M1 macrophage ratio, without detectable systemic toxicity in major organs. These findings establish a critical link between EC energy metabolism and immune microenvironment remodeling, providing a potentially translatable metabolic-engineering strategy for chronic diabetic wounds. This study opens new avenues for regenerative therapies targeting metabolic-immune interactions.

title: Chiral cerium doped nanoreactor-mediated bladder carcinoma reinforced ablation via fluorescence imaging navigated surgery along with photothermal strengthened ROS storm
abstract: Bladder cancer is regarded as one of the most prevalent malignant neoplasms of the urinary tract. However, the treatment of bladder cancer still presents unsatisfactory therapeutic outcomes, especially for advanced patients. Chiral nanomaterials hold significant prospect for elevating clinical therapeutic effect, thanks to their unparalleled chiral selectivity in biological-systems. In this work, we have engineered chiral a cerium oxide (CeO 2 ) doped mesoporous silica with, a photothermal and fluorescence contrast agent, indocyanine green loading (cSiCe&ICG). On account of the unique chiral nanostructure, this fascinating nanoreactor manifested effective enrichment in bladder tumor tissues and might be activated to mediate robust reactive oxygen species (ROS) under the weak acid and high H 2 O 2 microenvironment of the tumor regions. Owing to the accurate tumor targeting and fluorescence intensification, increased tumor-to-background ratio (TBR) had been achieved for accurately discriminating tumor tissues from surrounding normal tissue. With the navigation of fluorescence imaging at second near-infrared region (NIR II, 1000-1700 nm), tumors could be completely removed. In particularly, with the aid of 808 nm light irradiation, the chiral Ce-based nanoreactor exhibited a high catalytic efficiency, by integrating photothermal that further mediating ROS production via Ce ions for bladder tumor cell eradication. These findings underscored the prospect of chiral nanoreactor for efficacious fluorescence bioimaging for guiding tumor surgery and synergistic tumor eradiation especially with the assistance of NIR light activation.

title: Biomimetic nanocages with cascade homing for theranostics of ischemia-reperfusion acute kidney injury
abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) affects an estimated 13 million patients each year with a mortality of up to 1.7 million, yet current clinical management remains largely supportive and lacks etiology-directed therapy. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealed that mitochondrial dysfunction in proximal tubular cells is a hallmark of AKI pathology. Inspired by the regenerative capacity of axolotls, which relies on robust mitochondrial bioenergetics, we developed a biomimetic nanoplatform for treating AKI. We engineered GIPL nanoparticles comprising gold–silver nanocages loaded with the mitochondriotropic antioxidant idebenone (IDB), PEGylated for stability, and functionalized with LTH peptide for kidney injury molecule-1 (KIM-1) recognition. This design enables cascade targeting: cell-level targeting via KIM-1-mediated uptake into injured tubular epithelial cells, followed by subcellular accumulation of IDB in mitochondria. In vitro studies demonstrated that GIPL effectively scavenges reactive oxygen species, restores mitochondrial membrane potential, and inhibits apoptosis. Mechanistically, GIPL suppresses mTOR phosphorylation, thereby enhancing mitophagy to clear damaged mitochondria while attenuating pro-apoptotic signaling, ultimately restoring mitochondrial homeostasis.
