In vivo evaluation in Ischemia-reperfusion (IR) AKI mice confirmed preferential renal accumulation of GIPL, with significant amelioration of tubular injury, oxidative stress, and inflammation. The intrinsic X-ray attenuation of gold–silver nanocages additionally allows renal accumulation of GIPL to be visualized by computed tomography (CT). With a favorable biosafety profile, GIPL is a promising cascade-targeted mitochondrial therapy for IR-AKI. Drawing on the mitochondria-centric regenerative principle of the axolotl, this work integrates single-cell transcriptomic target identification, cascade cell-to-mitochondria delivery, and intrinsic CT contrast into a single nanoplatform, providing a new therapeutic strategy for AKI.

title: Supramolecular self-assembled nanomedicine targeting fatty acid metabolism to potentiate ferroptosis-enhanced photoimmunotherapy in triple-negative breast cancer
abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) presents a serious therapeutic challenge, largely owing to its metabolic adaptability and the immunosuppressive nature of its tumor microenvironment (TME). Photodynamic therapy (PDT) can cause oxidative injury and induce immunogenic cell death (ICD); however, its antitumor activity is often limited by inadequate reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation and weak immune activation. To address these barriers, a supramolecular self-assembled nanoplatform, termed OC@cRGD, was constructed through the co-assembly of the fatty acid synthase (FASN) inhibitor orlistat and the photosensitizer chlorin e6 (Ce6), followed by cyclic RGD (cRGD) modification to support integrin-mediated tumor targeting. This self-assembled design allows high drug loading and links metabolic interference with redox stress in a single nanoscale formulation. At the mechanistic level, orlistat disturbs lipid homeostasis and reduces the saturated fatty acid–based protection that helps TNBC cells resist membrane peroxidation. In parallel, light-activated PDT delivers a spatially restricted oxidative burst. After laser irradiation, these two processes act together to drive extensive iron-dependent lipid peroxidation, along with reduced GPX4 and FASN expression, thereby increasing cellular susceptibility to ferroptosis. This ferroptosis-reinforced PDT further induces pronounced ICD. In 4T1 tumor-bearing mice, OC@cRGD combined with laser irradiation inhibited tumor growth and reshaped the immune microenvironment, as reflected by dendritic cell maturation, M1-like macrophage polarization, and increased CD8 + T-cell infiltration. Overall, this work combines metabolic intervention with photoimmunotherapy and offers a metabolism-guided strategy for the development of self-assembled nanotherapeutics.

title: Aged microenvironment-triggered nanoreactors rejuvenate senescent LepR+ cells to remodel aged bone marrow
abstract: The senescence of leptin receptor-positive (LepR + ) cells in bone marrow contributes to the development of the aged bone marrow microenvironment, and rescuing LepR + cell senescence holds promise for alleviating age-related osteoporosis. This study reveals that senescent LepR + cells establish a pro-senescent vicious cycle driven by decreased NO, reduced Mg 2+ , and continuously accumulated reactive oxygen species (ROS). To break this cycle, we constructed an aged microenvironment-triggered nanoreactor capable of releasing NO/Mg 2+ and scavenging ROS to reverse cellular senescence. In this system, the nanoreactor (LPM) was fabricated via a thin-film hydration method, in which L-arginine was loaded into methoxy poly(ethylene glycol)-block-poly(propylene sulfide) (mPEG-b-PPS) and stabilized by Mg 2+ -mediated crosslinking. Coating LPM with senescent LepR + cell membranes generated CLPM, which exhibited superior targeting to LepR + cells, efficient NO/Mg 2+ release, and potent ROS scavenging activity. CLPM treatment effectively rejuvenated senescent LepR + cells, as evidenced by reduced senescence phenotypes and enhanced bone marrow regeneration. RNA sequencing further confirmed that CLPM disrupted the vicious cycle in senescent LepR + cells and remodeled the aged bone marrow. Collectively, our findings suggest that the CLPM nanoreactor offers a promising approach for rejuvenation of the aging skeletal system.

title: A biomimetic gas-protein co-delivery nanoplatform targets mitochondrial stress and GSDME activation for glioblastoma immunotherapy
abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) remains one of the most aggressive primary brain malignancies, with the therapeutic efficacy of conventional treatments and cancer immunotherapy being severely hindered by the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and the highly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Although pyroptosis, an inflammatory form of programmed cell death, can elicit potent antitumor immunity through the release of damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs), the precise induction of pyroptosis and the amplification of its immunostimulatory effects remain major challenges. Herein, we developed a biomimetic microglial cell membrane-coated nanosystem (M@GM) that integrates brain-targeted delivery, mitochondria-mediated damage, and innate immune activation for cascade-enhanced glioblastoma therapy. The nanosystem consists of a manganese carbonyl (MnCO) core loaded with Gasdermin E (GSDME) and cloaked with a microglial cell membrane, enabling efficient BBB penetration and active GBM targeting. Upon accumulation within the tumor microenvironment, M@GM responsively releases CO, Mn 2+ , and GSDME. CO and Mn 2+ induced mitochondrial stress and ROS accumulation, which were accompanied by activation of the Caspase-3/GSDME axis and pyroptosis-associated cell death. The associated HMGB1 release and CRT exposure are consistent with an immunogenic cell death (ICD)-related response, while Mn 2+ cooperatively activates the cGAS-STING innate immune pathway, promoting dendritic cell maturation, effector T-cell infiltration, and M1 polarization of tumor-associated macrophages, ultimately converting the immunologically “cold” GBM microenvironment into an immune-active “hot” phenotype. Both in vitro and in vivo studies demonstrated enhanced BBB transport and brain accumulation of M@GM, significantly inhibited GBM progression, prolonged the survival of tumor-bearing mice, and exhibited favorable biosafety. This work presents a biomimetic therapeutic strategy based on “biomimetic delivery-pyroptosis amplification-immune remodeling”, providing a promising design paradigm for brain-targeted nanomedicine-enabled cancer immunotherapy.

title: Engineered peroxisomes and patient-derived iPSC models as potential biomaterial platforms for precision neuroprotection in oxidative stress-driven central nervous system disorders
abstract: Peroxisomes couple hydrogen peroxide metabolism to lipid homeostasis, making their functions relevant to neurological disease and to the design of intracellular catalytic biomaterials. However, the strength of disease-specific evidence and the functions reproduced by current materials vary substantially. This narrative review distinguishes modified biological peroxisomes from artificial and biomimetic platforms and evaluates how patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) models could support their development. We examine membrane chemistry, substrate permeability, enzyme retention, catalytic activity, cell targeting, blood-brain barrier transport, three-dimensional tissue penetration, and intracellular fate. We separate the established causal role of peroxisomal defects in primary peroxisomal disorders from associative or unresolved findings in Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. Kleefstra syndrome is discussed as a hypothesis-generating neurodevelopmental model, without assuming a primary peroxisomal defect. Published artificial-organelle studies establish selected catalytic and delivery capabilities, but do not validate the integrated patient-specific CNS therapeutic strategy proposed here. We therefore outline a staged evaluation framework that combines materials characterization with mechanistic controls, differentiated neural cultures, multicellular models, animal pharmacology, safety, and manufacturing assessment. Comparison with conventional antioxidant carriers, plasmalogen supplementation, and PPAR agonists should determine whether compartmentalized catalysis offers a measurable advantage. We provide a platform classification, a disease-resolved evidence hierarchy, and a set of controls and measurable endpoints intended to make peroxisome-inspired constructs comparable across studies. Clinical development will require evidence of disease-relevant benefit beyond ROS reduction and an acceptable therapeutic window.

title: Synergistically reinforced bioresorbable hydrogel for mechanical–biological decoupling and osteogenic–angiogenic coupling
abstract: Ideal hydrogels for craniofacial bone regeneration should combine mechanical robustness, tunable bioresorption, and synergistic osteogenic-angiogenic bioactivity. However, conventional hydrogels suffer from an inherent trade-off between mechanical performance and biological activity, since both properties are dominated by crosslinking density. Here, a synergistically reinforced bioresorbable hydrogel system is developed by integrating highly ordered melt electrowriting poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) microfibrous scaffolds with bioactive glass (BG)-reinforced and functionalized gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA) matrix. This architectural reinforcement provides a strategy for partial mechanical-biological decoupling, enabling mechanical properties to be tailored independently of hydrogel crosslinking while preserving the bioactivity of the GelMA phase. The composite hydrogel efficiently promotes osteogenic differentiation of rat bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells and enhances angiogenic activities of human umbilical vein endothelial cells. The enrichment of Ras/MAPK signaling suggests a potential bifunctional role of this pathway in osteogenic and angiogenic regulation. In a rat critical-sized calvarial defect model, the scaffold remarkably induces extensive vascularized bone regeneration, achieving a bone volume fraction of 59.9 ± 7.4% at 12 weeks post-implantation. This work establishes a synergistic reinforcement strategy that decouples mechanical and biological functions while orchestrating osteogenic-angiogenic coupling for craniofacial bone regeneration.

title: 3D-printed fish-skin-derived composite dECM hydrogel patch for immunomodulatory and pro-angiogenic diabetic wound repair
abstract: Diabetic wounds are sustained by persistent inflammation, oxidative stress, infection susceptibility, and impaired angiogenesis, highlighting the need for bioactive dressings with manufacturable architectures. Here, we developed a methacrylation-free and photopolymerization-free fish-derived composite decellularized extracellular matrix (dECM) hydrogel scaffold by blending tilapia skin-derived dECM (TdECM) with carp skin-derived dECM (CdECM). Rheology-guided screening identified TdECM/CdECM-2, a 1:2 (v/v) blend of TdECM and CdECM, as a printable formulation that combined shear-thinning behavior, thermally induced collagen fibrillogenesis, and extrusion printability. Post-print stabilization with 1-ethyl-3-(3-dimethylaminopropyl)carbodiimide (EDC) and N-hydroxysuccinimide (NHS) preserved lattice architecture and generated highly porous scaffolds with a porosity of 90.3 ± 3.9%. In vitro , the composite scaffold (TdECM/CdECM-2) supported fibroblast, keratinocyte, and endothelial cell growth; promoted keratinocyte migration and endothelial network formation; and reduced Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa survival to 10.5 ± 1.3% and 13.3 ± 3.3%, respectively, in direct-contact assays. Macrophage studies indicated attenuated pro-inflammatory gene expression, increased pro-regenerative macrophage-associated markers, and reduced oxidative stress-associated reactive oxygen species accumulation. In mice with streptozotocin-induced diabetes, TdECM/CdECM-2 increased wound closure to 91.2 ± 3.9% at day 14, compared with 73.2 ± 9.7% in the untreated control and 79.3 ± 12.5% in the porcine skin-derived dECM (PdECM) group, together with improved re-epithelialization, collagen deposition, and cluster of differentiation 31 (CD31)-positive neovascularization, and reduced inflammatory myeloid cell accumulation and macrophage activation. Exploratory single-cell transcriptomic profiling suggested treatment-associated modulation of immune and stromal/endothelial gene programs related to inflammation and angiogenesis. These findings support fish-derived composite dECM scaffolds as printable bioactive wound dressing platforms for diabetic wound repair.

title: High-dose cerium dioxide nanorods induce behavioral and electroencephalographic abnormalities through 5-HT1B receptor signaling disruption with an evaluation of anpirtoline's therapeutic potential
abstract: Cerium dioxide nanorods (CeO 2 NRs) have drawn extensive research attention in the past few years for their exceptional generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and intrinsic catalytic properties. The two ends of the biological effect show a dose-dependent difference: protection of cells at low doses and damage to cells at high doses. Although the above processes are well documented in other biological contexts, the neurotoxicity induced by acute exposure to CeO 2 NRs, as well as its mechanism and possible prevention strategies, have yet to be elucidated. In the present study, we have found that CeO 2 NRs at a concentration of 300 μg/mL or higher induced neuronal apoptosis and reduced cell viability in vitro. After intranasal instillation in mice, CeO 2 NRs accumulated in the lysosomes and nuclei of neurons in the hippocampus and striatum. There was an increase in these abnormal exploratory behaviors, heightened seizure susceptibility, and altered electroencephalographic (EEG) oscillations. Integrated transcriptomic and proteomic profiling further indicated disruption of serotonin (5-HT) metabolism, caused by a downregulation of the 5-HT1B receptor, and thus provided a possible molecular mechanism for the behaviors and EEG abnormalities observed. Considerable changes also occurred in the various serotonergic mediators, neuronal excitability indicators, and inflammatory markers. Pharmacological activation of the 5-HT1B receptor with anpirtoline partially reversed the behaviors and EEG changes induced by CeO 2 NRs.

title: Corrigendum to “A study on extracellular and cellular composition to advance towards the rational design of contractile human myocardium” [Mater. Today Bio 40 (2026) 103647]
authors: Ana María Sánchez de la Nava

title: Corrigendum to “Procyanidin capsules attenuate PI3K/AKT-mediated mitochondrial dysfunction and accelerate skin wound healing in diabetic mice” [Materials Today Bio 38 (2026) 103029]
Corrigendum to “Selection of a novel MSC-targeted aptamer Pt-1 and its functionalized hydrogel for tissue regeneration” [39 (2026) 8]
Synergistic photothermal and antioxidant effects of chiral gold helical nanorods @CeO2 nanomaterials for accelerated infected wound healing
abstract: ABSTRACT: Bacterial infection is a major cause that impedes wound healing. Conventional antibiotic-based treatments, while aimed at suppressing infections, often lead to the emergence of drug resistance. Furthermore, monotherapeutic strategies are frequently inadequate in managing the accompanying inflammation and oxidative stress that follow infection. This work developed chiral gold helical nanorods (AuHNRs)@CeO 2 nanomaterials with photothermal bactericidal and reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging capabilities. D-AuHNRs@CeO 2 exhibited chiral-selective bioactivity, which preferentially entered damaged L929 mouse fibroblasts cells under oxidative stress, scavenged intracellular ROS, and enhanced wound healing by upregulating Catalase (CAT), transforming growth factor-beta 1 (TGF-β1) in L929 cells, and matrix metalloproteinase-1 (MMP1) in human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs). Additionally, it effectively shifted RAW264.7 mouse macrophages from the pro-inflammatory M1 phenotype to the pro-repair M2 phenotype, fostering an anti-inflammatory, pro-repair immune microenvironment. Compared with L- and DL- counterparts, D-AuHNRs@CeO 2 showed superior antibacterial and intracellular antioxidant performance. In a mouse model of infected wounds, D-AuHNRs@CeO 2 markedly accelerated wound healing and reduced local bacterial burden, highlighting its multifunctional synergistic therapeutic potential. This work presents a novel nanoplatform for the effective management of infected wounds. Statement of Significance Wound healing is often hindered by a vicious cycle of bacterial infection, excessive inflammation, and oxidative stress. Here, chiral gold helical nanorods decorated with regenerative CeO 2 (AuHNRs@CeO 2 ) was developed. This platform leverages stereoselective interactions to enhance bacterial targeting, converts near-infrared light into heat for photothermal sterilization, and scavenges pathological reactive oxygen species to relieve oxidative stress and inflammation. By integrating multiple therapeutic modalities into one system, this work directly tackles the complex challenge of bacterial wound infection and the subsequent oxidative stress.

title: Engineering exosomes-mediated RNA delivery regulates bone homeostasis and alleviates osteoporosis
abstract: Osteoporosis is characterized by dysregulated bone remodeling driven by excessive osteoclast-mediated bone resorption and insufficient osteoblast-mediated bone formation, often exacerbated by chronic inflammation and oxidative stress. Current pharmacological therapies remain limited by suboptimal efficacy and adverse effects, highlighting the need for alternative strategies that restore bone homeostasis. Here, we developed a bone-targeted, multifunctional exosome-based therapeutic platform by engineering M2 macrophage-derived exosomes co-loaded with platinum nanoparticles (Pt NPs) and a miR-196b inhibitor (BT-Exo-Pt-miR-196 inhibitor). The engineered exosomes exhibited preserved structural integrity, favorable biocompatibility, efficient bone-targeting capability, and excellent in vivo biosafety. Pt NPs endowed the system with robust reactive oxygen species (ROS)-scavenging activity, while M2-derived exosomes and miR-196b inhibition synergistically attenuated inflammatory cytokine expression. In vitro, BT-Exo-Pt-miR-196 inhibitor markedly enhanced osteogenic differentiation, extracellular matrix maturation, and mineralization through coordinated upregulation of osteogenic transcription factors and matrix proteins. Concurrently, osteoclastogenesis was significantly suppressed, as evidenced by reduced TRAP-positive multinucleated cells, impaired actin ring formation, and downregulation of NFATc1 and downstream osteoclast-associated markers. In an ovariectomy-induced osteoporosis mouse model, bone-targeted delivery of BT-Exo-Pt-miR-196 inhibitor effectively preserved trabecular bone microarchitecture, enhanced osteogenic activity, reduced osteoclast function, and alleviated bone loss without inducing systemic toxicity. Collectively, this study demonstrates that bone-targeted M2 macrophage-derived exosomes delivering a miR-196b inhibitor represent a promising immunomodulatory and gene-regulatory nanotherapeutic strategy for restoring bone homeostasis and treating osteoporosis.

title: EMSCs-derived exosomes rescue p75NTR−/− -mediated osteogenesis deficiency via PI3K/Akt/ERK1/2 signaling pathways
abstract: ABSTRACT The repair of the critical-sized bone defects remains a major challenge for orthopedic surgeons, particularly when osteogenesis is impaired by p75 neurotrophin receptor (p75NTR) deficiency. However, the underlying molecular mechanisms are not fully understood. This study aimed to clarify the role of p75NTR in bone regeneration and to develop a cell-free approach to rescue p75NTR −/− deficiency–mediated osteogenic deficiency through a controlled releasing of wild-type ectomesenchymal stem cells exosomes (WT-Exo) which were incorporated into silk fibroin/polycaprolactone 2:5 / polyvinyl alcohol (SF/PCL 2:5 /PVA) coaxial nanofibrous membranes. p75NTR −/− mice exhibited a reduced bone mass and delayed ossification, while WT-Exo–loaded membranes partially restored osteogenic deficiency in p75NTR −/− cells and enhanced expression of osteogenic markers such as alkaline phosphatase (ALP), collagen type I (Col-I), osteopontin (OPN) and runt-related transcription factor 2 (Runx2) aaccompanied by activating of phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)/protein kinase B (Akt)/extracellular signal-regulated kinase 1/2 (ERK1/2) signaling pathway. Following implantation of the WT-Exo–loaded membranes into the critical-sized cranial defects in p75NTR −/− mice, new bone formation in the defect site was significantly improved by a sustained release of WT-Exo. Overall, the findings in this study highlighted the critical role of p75NTR in osteogenic differentiation of ectomesenchymal stem cells (EMSCs) and demonstrated that WT-Exo, delivered via the coaxial electrospun membranes, represented an effective cell-free intervention method to reverse bone formation deficiency caused by p75NTR deficiency, providing a promising strategy for gene deficiency–related bone diseases.

title: Microneedle-mediated co-delivery of biomimetic melanin and pro-regenerative factors for oxidative and immune modulation in vitiligo
abstract: Vitiligo lesions are characterized by elevated epidermal oxidative stress, cytotoxic immune activation, and impaired melanogenesis, while conventional topical therapies often fail to modulate these pathogenic events due to limited skin penetration and therapeutic depth. To address these challenges, a dual-layer gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA)/hyaluronic acid methacryloyl (HAMA)//hyaluronic acid (HA) (Gel//HA) microneedle system was engineered. The inner HA layer rapidly dissolves upon insertion, releasing keratinocyte-membrane-coated artificial melanin nanoparticles (MPDA) to achieve early reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging and targeted delivery to keratinocytes. The outer Gel hydrogel layer enables sustained intradermal delivery of basic fibroblast growth factor (bFGF) and tyrosinase (TYR), supporting melanocyte survival and restoring melanin synthesis. The microneedles exhibited robust mechanical strength (0.234 ± 0.014 N/needle) with a penetration depth of approximately 300-350 μm. In vitro , the cumulative release of bFGF and TYR reached 65% and 70% within the first 72 h, respectively, and subsequently increased more gradually to 92.1% and 90.7% by day 21. In vitro , the combined administration of MPDA, bFGF, and TYR, mitigated H 2 O 2 -induced oxidative injury and enhanced keratinocyte viability. In a monobenzone-induced mouse model, Gel@bFGF/TYR//HA@MPDA treatment markedly promoted repigmentation, restored epidermal melanin deposition, and reduced the expression of CD8, IFN-γ, and TNF-α. Transcriptomic analysis further revealed suppression of ferroptosis-related genes and reactivation of the Wnt–Frizzled–MITF melanogenic signaling axis. This spatially designed microneedle system provides coordinated antioxidant, immunomodulatory, and pro-melanogenic effects, offering a promising localized therapeutic strategy for vitiligo.

title: In situ-forming manganese-curcumin nanozyme film promotes diabetic wound healing via photothermal antibacterial and anti-inflammatory actions
abstract: Oxidative stress, bacterial infection, and persistent inflammatory responses are key inhibitory factors for chronic wound healing, yet most conventional dressings fail to simultaneously address these pathological barriers. This study presents a multifunctional composite film incorporating manganese-curcumin (Mn-Cur) nanozymes prepared via a facile, carrier-free synthesis. These nanozymes exhibit dual superoxide dismutase (SOD)- and catalase (CAT)-mimetic activities, enabling efficient elimination of superoxide anion radicals (•O 2 - ) and hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ). A rapid Prussian blue (PB) coating is introduced onto the Mn-Cur surface to enhance biocompatibility and confer photothermal antibacterial capability, forming Mn-Cur@PB (MC@PB) nanocomposites. The engineered nanozymes efficiently scavenge excess reactive oxygen species (ROS), exert potent antibacterial activity, and attenuate pro-inflammatory macrophage activation while inducing an immunoregulatory phenotype. The MC@PB nanocomposites are subsequently incorporated into a silk fibroin (SF)/polyvinyl butyral (PVB) matrix and cast into an in situ-forming wound dressing (denoted SPMP), bridging nanomaterial design and practical wound management. In vivo evaluation using infected diabetic wound models confirms that, under near-infrared (NIR) irradiation, the SPMP dressing effectively eliminates bacteria, alleviates inflammation, facilitates collagen deposition and angiogenesis, and accelerates wound closure. This multifunctional SPMP film represents a promising candidate for clinical chronic wound treatment.

title: Novel modifications of small extracellular vesicles to enhance cardiac-specific delivery of siPKA RNA and edaravone against ischemia-reperfusion cardiac injury
abstract: Relative tight endothelium in the heart may be a barrier for drugs in the large molecule and nanoparticle formats to act on cardiomyocytes. We hypothesize that enhanced binding of large molecules or nanoparticles to the cardiac capillary endothelial cells can increase the transendothelial transport of these drugs to exert their effects on the cardiomyocytes beneath the endothelium. CD36 is densely localized on the membrane of myocardial endothelial cells and thus we engineered small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) to be coated with an analog of CD36 ligand fatty acids, KOdiA-PC. Further to trap more therapeutic sEVs in the myocardium, we conjugated the sEVs with ischemic myocardium- targeting peptide (IMT). These dual-modifications of sEVs resulted in markedly enhanced fluorescent retention in the MIRI heart, indicating the potential of this system as a promising drug delivery platform for ischemic myocardium. Thus we loaded the dually-modified sEVs with edaravone (EDV) and siPKA RNA to dampen the ROS and inhibit overactivated PKA in myocardium subjected to ischemia/reperfusion injury, making a multistage-targeting and multifunctional sEVs delivery system (KI-sEVs/siPKA/EDV). The results showed that KOdiA-PC modification significantly enhanced sEVs transendothelial transport efficiency, and dual-targeting modification dramatically increased the accumulation of sEVs in the heart. Intravenous injection of KI-sEVs/siPKA/EDV significantly decreased myocardial infarction size, improved cardiac function and reduced cardiac fibrosis in animals subjected to MIRI or MI. KI-sEVs/siPKA/EDV also showed good biocompatibility and low toxicity. Our study provides an innovative cardiac-targeting delivery strategy and offers a promising method for MIRI and Persistent coronary occlusion MI treatment.

title: Covalently integrated curcumin turns piperazine-based polyurethane-urea into a scaffold-as-drug for infected bone repair
abstract: Infected bone defects are difficult to repair because bacterial persistence, excessive inflammation, oxidative stress, and impaired osteogenesis occur simultaneously. Conventional drug-loaded scaffolds often rely on physical loading, which can cause burst release and premature drug depletion. Here, we developed a scaffold-as-drug platform by covalently integrating curcumin (CUR) into a 3D-printable piperazine-based polyurethane-urea (P-PUU) backbone. CUR served as a reactive phenolic chain extender, while piperazine provided urea-forming structural segments. Spectroscopic and chromatographic analyses supported polymer formation and CUR incorporation, and molecular simulations indicated reduced chain mobility and stronger interchain association after CUR integration. The resulting CUR-P-PUU scaffolds retained interconnected porosity, improved apparent wettability, enhanced mechanical performance, and provided sustained degradation-associated CUR availability. Although physically blended CUR/P-PUU showed stronger short-term osteogenic responses in vitro , consistent with greater early CUR availability, CUR-P-PUU exhibited a more sustained CUR-availability profile during scaffold degradation. CUR-P-PUU supported BMSC viability, inhibited methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), suppressed LPS-induced inflammatory cytokines, and promoted osteogenic differentiation. In a rat MRSA-infected calvarial defect model, CUR-P-PUU reduced bacterial burden, was associated with a less inflammatory and more pro-reparative local immune phenotype, and enhanced bone formation and mineralization. This study establishes covalent small-molecule integration as a materials-driven strategy for infection-resilient bone regeneration in a printable biodegradable scaffold.

title: A graphdiyne-enabled TiO2/g-C3N4 bio-heterojunction for visible-light antibacterial photocatalysis and infected wound healing
abstract: Visible-light-driven antibacterial photocatalysis holds great promise for infected wound management; however, efficient and biologically compatible heterointerfaces remain limited. Here, we constructed a graphdiyne-enabled TiO 2 /g-C 3 N 4 based bio-heterojunction (TCN/GDY) by growing graphdiyne (GDY) onto a TiO 2 /g-C 3 N 4 scaffold, which couples enhanced visible-light harvesting with antibacterial wound therapy. Structural characterization, photoelectrochemical measurements, valence band analysis, in situ XPS, electron paramagnetic resonance, and density functional theory support interfacial electronic coupling, an enhanced photoresponse, and reactive oxygen species generation. These observations are consistent with a proposed dual S-scheme like mechanism. Under 420 nm LED irradiation, TCN/GDY achieved >99% elimination of Escherichia coli , 99.40 ± 0.34% elimination of Staphylococcus aureus , and 98.65 ± 0.74% elimination of methicillin-resistant S. aureus ( MRSA ), and reduced retained crystal-violet-stained MRSA biofilm biomass by 78.57 ± 2.38% under the tested treatment and washing conditions. Multi-omics analysis identified treatment associated changes in central metabolism and nutrient transport. In an MRSA -infected mouse wound model, visible-light-activated TCN/GDY reduced the bacterial burden by 97.98 ± 1.04% and decreased the residual wound area to 2.93 ± 1.46% by day 11. This study establishes a graphdiyne-enabled TiO 2 /g-C 3 N 4 -based bio-heterojunction as a visible-light antibacterial photocatalytic platform for infected wound healing.

title: A stretchable liquid-metal bioelectric catheter for active management of catheter-associated urinary tract infections
abstract: Catheter-associated urinary tract infections (CAUTIs) continue to be a major clinical complication of indwelling catheterization, sustained by persistent bacterial colonization and dysregulated local immune responses. Most antimicrobial coatings provide passive protection and have limited capacity to address both bacterial persistence and the host response at the catheter–tissue interface. This study presents a stretchable urological catheter for electrical stimulation (SUCES) based on a liquid metal composite. SUCES consists of a stable gallium-10 vol.% silver (Ga-Ag) circuit encapsulated within a silver-doped (5 vol.%) polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS-Ag) layer. SUCES delivers low-voltage electrical stimulation (1.5 V for 5 min) in combination with sustained Ag release, resulting in effective combined antibacterial activity. In vitro testing demonstrates bacterial killing efficiencies of approximately 95% for E. coli and 94% for S. aureus . The same electrical input also promoted an M1-associated macrophage response. In a rabbit CAUTI model, seven days of treatment reduced the viable urinary bacterial burden by 93% (>1-log reduction). SUCES-treated tissues also showed less infection-associated inflammation and better-preserved urothelial barrier integrity. These findings support SUCES as an active bioelectric catheter interface that integrates antibacterial treatment with macrophage-associated immune modulation for catheter-associated infection management.

title: Spatiotemporally coordinated immunometabolic-hyperthermia therapy for diabetic bone defect regeneration
abstract: Diabetic bone defects (DBDs) are typified by persistent inflammation, oxidative stress, and microbial infection within the diabetic microenvironment, which collectively hinder osteogenesis and angiogenesis. Herein, we introduce an Immunometabolic-Hyperthermia Therapy (IMHT) strategy based on a dual-functional nanoplatform, namely a polydopamine/itaconate-incorporated agarose/gelatin (PIAG) hydrogel. This system is fabricated by incorporating itaconic acid (ITA) into polydopamine (PDA) nanoparticles through in situ polymerization, followed by encapsulation within a gelatin/agarose matrix. ITA primarily provides immunometabolic regulation, while PDA enables a tunable photothermal response. Upon localized photothermal heating (∼50 °C), the PIAG hydrogel effectively disrupts bacterial biofilms, with photothermal treatment providing the dominant antibacterial effect and ITA offering an additional supportive contribution. Upon mild photothermal activation (∼41 °C), IMHT mitigates excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, inhibits neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation, and reprograms macrophages toward an M2-like reparative phenotype through JAK1/STAT1 pathway inhibition. The resulting pro-regenerative immune milieu enhances fibroblast growth factor-2 (FGF-2) secretion, while heat-induced activation of HSP90 stabilizes FGF-2/FGFR1 signaling, further promoting osteogenic differentiation and endothelial migration. Overall, the spatiotemporally coordinated antibacterial, immunometabolic, and regenerative regulation realized by IMHT offers a comprehensive and effective strategy for the repair of diabetic bone defects.

title: A pro-regenerative petroleum jelly-based, copper-doped bioactive glass ointment for impaired wound healing in metabolic syndrome
abstract: Abstract Chronic wound healing is often impaired in conditions such as metabolic syndrome, requiring effective therapeutic interventions to promote tissue regeneration and repair. In this study, we evaluated the wound healing potential of petroleum jelly (P Jelly)-based bioactive glass ointments (PBGCu) with varying copper concentrations (0, 1, and 3 wt%) in both in vitro and in vivo models of wound healing. PBGCu formulations demonstrated high biocompatibility with human dermal fibroblasts (HDF) and human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVEC). Additionally, PBGCu ointments exhibited strong antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus , suggesting their utility for the care of chronic wounds. In both metabolic syndrome mouse and pig models, PBGCu3-treated wounds showed significantly faster wound closure, enhanced epithelial regeneration, and increased dermal thickness compared to saline and P Jelly controls. Histological analysis also revealed 50% increased vascularization (p < 0.0001) and a 90% reduction in scar formation (p < 0.0001) in PBGCu3-treated wounds. These findings show that PBGCu formulations, especially at 3 wt% copper concentration, significantly improve wound healing by promoting epithelial regeneration, dermal tissue formation, and vascularization, while also offering antibacterial protection. The sustained Cu 2+ ions release from PBGCu ointments provides long-term support for tissue regeneration, positioning this ointment composition as a promising therapeutic tool for chronic wound management. Future studies will focus on elucidating the underlying mechanisms and evaluating the therapeutic efficacy of PBGCu formulations in infected wounds. Highlights Developed a Petroleum Jelly–based copper-doped bioactive glass ointment (PBGCu) enabling sustained and controlled Cu²⁺ ion release. PBGCu significantly accelerated wound closure and improved epithelial and dermal tissue regeneration. PBGCu enhanced hair follicle regeneration and tissue remodeling in full-thickness wounds. Validated therapeutic efficacy in both mouse and pig models that support translational relevance. Offers a simple, low-cost, and clinically adaptable topical formulation for metabolic syndrome-related wound complications.

title: Clinical validation of a vial wall-based dielectric barrier discharge plasma activation device for plasma-activated platelet-rich plasma preparation in osteoarthritis pain management
abstract: Cold atmospheric plasma (CAP) has significant potential in biomedical applications. However, conventional plasma activation requires electrodes to contact a liquid directly, exposing it to the external environment. This conflicts with sterile, closed preparations required clinically. A vial wall-based dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) plasma activation device addresses this need by using standard clinical blood collection tube walls as a dielectric barrier. Electrodes contact only the tube exterior, never the liquid inside, and activation requires simply inserting the tube into the reactor chamber. Applied to platelet-rich plasma (PRP) therapy for osteoarthritis (OA), the device produced plasma-activated PRP (PA-PRP) with enhanced platelet activation, increased levels of transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β; 24%), platelet-derived growth factor (PDGF; 37%), and insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1; 32%), and broadly upregulated anti-inflammatory cytokines. In the destabilization of the medial meniscus (DMM) mouse OA model, PA-PRP treatment was associated with improved gait parameters and lower cartilage degeneration scores relative to PRP treatment. Human OA cartilage explants showed greater matrix staining after PA-PRP treatment. In an exploratory, randomized, single-blind split-body study involving three patients, PA-PRP-treated knees, compared with contralateral PRP-treated knees, showed numerically larger improvements in visual analog scale (VAS) pain score, Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index (WOMAC) score, and effusion volume at week 15, with no adverse events during observation. These clinical observations are descriptive and hypothesis-generating, as the sample size precludes reliable efficacy or comparative safety inferences. Together, findings support device feasibility and PA-PRP use in OA and provide a rationale for adequately powered studies.

title: pH/ROS dual-responsive SmartGel-Cas9/TRPV4 for autophagy regulation in intervertebral disc degeneration
abstract: This study developed a pH/ROS dual-responsive SmartGel platform for local CRISPR-Cas9 RNP delivery and TRPV4 inhibition in intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD). The GelMA/PBA-based SmartGel responded to acidic and oxidative microenvironmental cues and released Cas9/sgRNA under disease-mimicking conditions. In nucleus pulposus (NP) cells, SmartGel-Cas9/TRPV4 lowered ROS accumulation, restored mitochondrial membrane potential (ΔΨm), and coordinated apoptosis, senescence, Ca 2+ homeostasis, CaMKKβ-dependent AMPK-mTOR signaling, and autophagic flux. CaMKKβ knockdown weakened AMPK-mTOR activation and autophagic-flux restoration, supporting CaMKKβ as a required link in this mechanism. In the rat IVDD model, the system preserved disc architecture, improved hydration status, reinforced extracellular matrix (ECM) homeostasis, and restrained downstream pathological signaling. Exploratory scRNA-seq and proteomic analyses further indicated treatment-associated shifts in Ca 2+ /autophagy/MAPK/Wnt-related programs. Overall, SmartGel-Cas9/TRPV4 may attenuate IVDD by restoring CaMKKβ-associated autophagic degradation and ECM balance while limiting aberrant signaling activation.

title: Sandwich-structured PVDF/protein piezoelectric hydrogel regulates osteogenesis and adipogenesis through glycerophospholipid metabolism in osteoporotic inflammatory bone defects
abstract: Osteoporosis can occur when age-related ovarian dysfunction leads to estrogen deficiency. When bone mineral content decreases, fragile bones are susceptible to bone defects. This estrogen deficiency causes differentiation of mesenchymal cells to shift towards adipogenesis and reduced osteogenesis, which culminates in nonunion. With the potential to modulate cell differentiation, electrical stimulation is promising for osteoporosis defects complicated by an inflammatory environment. A sandwich-structured silk fibroin hydrogel (RSF) with three layers of polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) membrane with many β-crystalline phases and MXene for electrical conductance was fabricated, generating voltages up to 500 mV to leverage the implanted bone grafts for a sustainable source of electrical stimulation. Combined transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses revealed that piezoelectric stimulation promoted osteogenesis and suppressed glycerophospholipid metabolism by upregulating lipid degradation-related genes. Specifically, Pla2g4a was critical to the hydrolysis of phospholipids, as shown by Sudan black B staining in rBMSCs. Finally, we created femoral defects in osteoporotic rats and implanted MXene/PVDF/RSF hydrogel to promote osteogenesis and reduce adipogenesis, as shown by micro-CT and immunostaining. As a result, piezoelectric MXene/PVDF/RSF hydrogel effectively redirected bone-fat balance and overcame the inflammatory environment in osteoporotic bone defects, serving future clinical applications.

title: A copper-based RNAi nanocomplex unleashes immunogenic ferroptosis by reversing metabolic adaptation and suppressing extracellular GPX4
abstract: ABSTRACT Ferroptosis is an immunogenic form of regulated cell death with considerable potential for cancer immunotherapy, yet its efficacy is frequently limited by adaptive resistance mechanisms. Here, we uncover a previously unrecognized bidirectional role of copper-based ferroptosis inducers in breast cancer. On the one hand, copper suppresses the release of extracellular GPX4, an immunosuppressive damage-associated molecular pattern, preserving the immunostimulatory effects of ferroptotic cell death. On the other hand, copper-induced ferroptotic stress activates carnitine palmitoyltransferase 1A (CPT1A)-dependent fatty acid oxidation, which limits polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) availability and reduces ferroptosis susceptibility. To overcome this adaptive metabolic resistance, we developed siC@CuPP, a polyethylenimine-modified copper-doped polypyrrole nanocomplex that delivers Cpt1a siRNA while retaining the intrinsic ferroptosis-inducing activity of the CuPPy core. siC@CuPP efficiently silenced Cpt1a , inhibited fatty acid oxidation-driven PUFA consumption, promoted lipid remodeling, and impaired NADPH replenishment, thereby enhancing oxidative stress and ferroptosis sensitivity. Concurrently, copper-mediated suppression of extracellular GPX4 relieved ferroptosis-associated immunosuppression and facilitated dendritic cell activation. These coordinated effects established a positive feedback loop between immunogenic ferroptosis and antitumor immunity through interferon-γ–ACSL4 signaling. In an orthotopic 4T1 triple-negative breast cancer model, systemic administration of siC@CuPP elicited robust antitumor immune responses, significantly suppressing primary tumor growth and pulmonary metastasis. Collectively, this work identifies CPT1A-dependent metabolic adaptation and extracellular GPX4-mediated immunosuppression as two notable barriers to immunogenic ferroptosis and provides a coordinated strategy for overcoming both, thereby amplifying ferroptosis-driven cancer immunotherapy.

title: Metal-based hydrogen-generating therapeutic systems: From reactive chemistry to route-specific exposure and translational design
abstract: Molecular hydrogen (H 2 ) has shown broad therapeutic relevance in oxidative injury, inflammation, metabolic dysfunction and tissue repair, yet its clinical translation remains limited by rapid diffusion, poor retention and a poorly defined dose–exposure relationship. Metal-based H 2 -generating systems offer an engineering strategy to produce or release H 2 at pathological sites or material–tissue interfaces, where local exposure can be shaped by material design. This review reframes these platforms as material–formulation–route–indication systems rather than isolated material classes. The field now extends from classical metal hydrides to broader metal-containing platforms that generate or release H 2 through hydrolysis, corrosion, electrochemical reactions or hydrogen storage-mediated release. Their therapeutic behavior is governed by route-specific exposure fields shaped by H 2 release, accompanying reaction chemistry, formulation-defined compartments and tissue environments. Accordingly, route-oriented evaluation is essential because the same reactive core can produce distinct exposure profiles, safety boundaries and translational requirements across oral, local, vascular and implantable contexts. Mechanistically, H 2 -dependent redox and cytoprotective biology provides an important entry point, but therapeutic outcomes arise from a multi-effector local chemical milieu involving metal-derived species, coupled physicochemical changes and, in some platforms, external activation. Translational development therefore requires controlled materials engineering, route-specific exposure metrics, mechanism-matched validation, a PK/PD-like exposure–response framework adapted for reactive material systems and manufacturing strategies aligned with chemistry, manufacturing and controls (CMC) requirements. The field should advance toward route-specific, exposure-defined and mechanism-validated local reaction therapy.

title: Hyaluronic acid-based nanoparticles in cancer diagnosis and therapy: Molecular weight matters
abstract: Hyaluronic acid (HA)-based nanomaterials have emerged as promising platforms for cancer therapy owing to their excellent biocompatibility, biodegradability, and intrinsic tumor-targeting capability. However, the intrinsic biological functions of HAs are profoundly affected by molecular weight (MW), a factor that remains underappreciated in current nanocarrier design. Accumulating evidence indicates that HA exhibits distinct MW-dependent functions that high MW HA (HMW-HA) primarily supports tissue homeostasis and anti-inflammatory signaling, whereas low MW (LMW-HA) and oligomeric HA (oligo-HA) act as bioactive mediators that promote inflammation, angiogenesis, and tumor progression. Currently, most HA-based drug delivery strategies continue to treat HA mainly as a passive carrier, largely neglecting its MW-dependent biological activity and its impact on therapeutic outcomes. To address this gap, this review proposes a MW-structure-function framework for the rational design of HA-based nanomedicines. We first summarize the MW-dependent biological behaviors of HA across physiological and pathological contexts, with a particular focus on its role in the tumor microenvironment (TME). We then examine how MW regulates nanoparticle self-assembly, physicochemical properties, and interactions with biological systems, thereby influencing biodistribution, cellular uptake, and therapeutic efficacy. Building on these insights, we highlight recent advances in MW-optimized HA nanoplatforms for tumor imaging and multimodal therapies, including chemotherapy, phototherapy, and immunotherapy. Lastly, we discuss the key challenges and future directions, emphasizing the need to integrate the intrinsic biological activity of HA into nanocarrier engineering. This review aims to redefine HA-based nanoparticles from passive delivery vehicles into programmable bioactive nanoplatforms, providing a conceptual foundation for next-generation cancer nanomedicine.

title: Targeting histone methylation with ROS nanoparticles delivering PARPi prodrugs to amplify the stimulation of cGAS-STING for immunotherapy in ovarian cancer
abstract: Poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors (PARPi) has improved survival in ovarian cancer (OC), yet its efficacy is severely compromised by the restoration of homologous recombination repair and enhanced drug efflux. Here, we report a reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive nanoparticle (DP@NP) for the co-delivery of PARPi and DOT1L inhibitor (DOT1Li) to overcome these limitations through a dual-function mechanism. DP@NP can be triggered by ROS in cancer cells, whereupon the released PARPi induces DNA damage, while DOT1Li augments DNA damage accumulation by suppressing PARPi efflux and impairing DNA repair. This coordinated dual action promotes the accumulation of cytosolic double-stranded DNA, thereby robustly activating the cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) pathway. In vivo , DP@NP exhibits efficient tumor targeting and elicits pronounced antitumor activity across multiple OC models. Notably, it remodels the tumor immune microenvironment and upregulates PD-L1, thereby significantly enhancing tumor responsiveness to immune checkpoint inhibitors. This study presents a co-delivery strategy that enhances PARPi efficacy while concurrently promoting antitumor immune activation, offering a viable avenue for the treatment of OC.

title: Triaptosis-based biomimetic nanoparticle for the treatment of oral squamous cell carcinoma lymph node metastasis
abstract: Lymph node metastasis (LNM) is a major determinant of poor prognosis in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) and remains difficult to treat due to the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment and limited response to immune checkpoint blockade. Here, we report a biomimetic nanotherapeutic platform designed to induce triaptosis and enhance antitumor immunity for the treatment of metastatic OSCC. Semaglutide-loaded cerium oxide nanoparticles were engineered and further coated with macrophage membranes to construct Semg@Ce@MM, enabling improved tumor targeting and immune compatibility. The nanoplatform exerts dual therapeutic actions: cerium-mediated pro-oxidative activity triggers VPS34-associated triaptosis characterized by cytoplasmic vacuolization, while semaglutide activates MAPK signaling to enhance tumor cell susceptibility to death. In vitro studies demonstrate potent antitumor activity, including inhibition of tumor cell proliferation and invasion. In an orthotopic lymph node metastasis model, Semg@Ce@MM significantly suppresses metastatic tumor growth, promotes dendritic cell maturation, increases CD4 + and CD8 + T cell infiltration, and reprograms tumor-associated macrophages toward a pro-inflammatory phenotype. Importantly, Semg@Ce@MM synergizes with anti-PD-L1 therapy to overcome resistance to immune checkpoint blockade while maintaining favorable biosafety. This work establishes a triaptosis-based nanomedicine strategy for the treatment of metastatic OSCC and highlights a promising combinatorial approach that integrates oxidative stress mediated cell death with cancer immunotherapy.

title: An ibuprofen-eluting electrospun membrane prevents ureteral fibrosis by dampening macrophage-associated fibroblast activation
abstract: Background Ureteral stricture is driven by unresolved inflammation and progressive matrix deposition, yet mechanism-guided local therapies remain limited. Methods We integrated spatial transcriptomics of human normal and stricture ureters with an in-house scRNA-seq reference generated from three stricture specimens and independently evaluated annotation using the normal ureter dataset GSE194129. Urothelial injury-conditioned medium (UICM), primary ureteral fibroblasts, and THP-1-derived macrophages were used to model epithelial-immune-stromal signaling. An ibuprofen-functionalized PCL/gelatin electrospun membrane (P/G-PLL-IBU) was characterized and tested in a rabbit ureteral thermal-injury model. Results Spatial analysis identified a fibro-inflammatory niche with co-enrichment of fibroblast and macrophage programs in stenotic regions. Low normal-reference feature spots displayed cytoskeletal remodeling-associated signatures. UICM contained increased IL-6 and HMGB1 and elevated LDH release, induced an inflammatory fibroblast-like state, and produced a macrophage activation state dominated by pro-inflammatory features. Conditioned medium from UICM-activated macrophages enhanced FN1, COL1A1, α-SMA, and Smad2/3 phosphorylation in UICM-primed fibroblasts. Soluble ibuprofen suppressed macrophage NF-κB/COX-2-associated activation, and conditioned medium from treated cultures elicited lower profibrotic responses in fibroblasts. PGE 2 add-back partially restored these responses. P/G-PLL-IBU preserved nanofibrous architecture, released ibuprofen for 56 days, and showed favorable hemocompatibility and cytocompatibility. In rabbits, P/G-PLL-IBU reduced early and long-term collagen deposition and upper urinary tract dilation for up to 90 days. Delayed membrane placement produced no detectable reversal of established fibrosis within the 30-day post-treatment observation window. Conclusion Together, human spatial mapping and stepwise in vitro analyses link macrophage activation to fibroblast Smad2/3-associated remodeling in ureteral stricture, and local ibuprofen delivery via electrospun membrane can blunt this trajectory after ureteral injury.

title: Targeted delivery of celastrol and siRNA via macrophage biomimetic nanoparticles for doxorubicin-induced cardiomyopathy therapy
abstract: Doxorubicin-induced cardiomyopathy (DIC) is a severe complication following anthracycline chemotherapy, and its main pathogenesis is inflammatory responses and ferroptosis. This study constructed hyaluronic acid-based macrophage biomimetic nanoparticles (M@HCDA) to co-delivery of Celastrol (Cel) and siADAM17 for the treatment of DIC. This research revealed that Cel exerted an anti-ferroptosis effect by regulating GPX4 and SLC7A11, while siADAM17 inhibited TAK1-MAPK pathway activation by silencing ADAM17. Meanwhile, the synergistic effect of Cel and siADAM17 significantly alleviated oxidative stress, myocardial fibrosis, apoptosis, and mitochondrial dysfunction, thereby relieving myocardial injury caused by DOX-induced cardiotoxicity and providing effective early cardioprotection. In vitro and in vivo experiments indicated that M@HCDA exhibited good stability, biocompatibility, and targeting capability, showing the clinical application potential. The design and development of M@HCDA provide new experimental evidence and candidate strategy for treating DIC.

title: Extracellular matrix ageing as a biological variable in 3D cancer models: A framework for age-aware model design
abstract: Ageing is a major determinant of cancer risk and outcome, yet age-associated changes in the extracellular matrix (ECM) remain poorly represented in most preclinical cancer models. Throughout life, the ECM undergoes alterations in composition, architecture, biochemical modification, mechanics and turnover that influence cell behaviour and tissue function. Although advanced three-dimensional (3D) cancer models increasingly incorporate ECM components, ageing is rarely considered as an independent biological variable, and the terms aged, ageing-associated and age-mimetic ECM are often applied to biologically distinct experimental systems. Here, we review current evidence describing ECM remodelling across the lifespan and evaluate how age-associated matrix states have been incorporated into 3D cancer models. We propose a framework that distinguishes four principal modelling strategies: chronologically aged ECM models, defined age-associated ECM modification models, cell-mediated ECM remodelling models, and mixed multicomponent ageing models. These approaches differ substantially in the ageing-associated features they reproduce, the degree of biological fidelity they provide and the strength of mechanistic inference they permit. Analysis of published studies provides evidence that age-associated ECM states can influence tumour invasion, proliferation, signalling and therapeutic response across many cancer types. At the same time, the available evidence indicates that ECM ageing is a multidimensional process that no single molecular or mechanical surrogate can capture. Hence, we argue that age-aware cancer models should be classified and interpreted according to the specific ageing-associated ECM features they reproduce and experimentally validate. By establishing ECM ageing as a definable biological variable, this framework provides practical guidance for designing, validating, and interpreting next-generation age-aware 3D in vitro cancer models.

title: Rewiring cholesterol vulnerabilities with biomaterials: Mechanisms and opportunities for cancer therapy
abstract: Tumor progression is accompanied by adaptive metabolic rewiring that extends beyond energy and amino acid metabolism to lipid networks. Among these alterations, disrupted cholesterol homeostasis has emerged as a key driver of tumor proliferation, migration, invasion, chemoresistance and immune escape. Cholesterol metabolism also shapes immune cell function, thereby linking tumor-intrinsic metabolic adaptation to immune remodeling in the tumor microenvironment. Recent advances in biomaterial-based therapeutics have expanded the scope of cholesterol-targeted cancer therapy. This Review summarizes how engineered biomaterials regulate cholesterol supply and uptake, intracellular cholesterol trafficking, membrane organization and cholesterol oxidation, and how these strategies reshape tumor cell survival, therapeutic resistance and antitumor immunity. We further discuss the integration of cholesterol-targeted biomaterials with chemotherapy, photodynamic therapy, sonodynamic therapy and immunotherapy, as well as key translational challenges, including metabolic compensation, preservation of cholesterol balance in normal tissues, the context-dependent biological effects of sterol products and the need for product-resolved analysis, since changes in total cholesterol or ROS alone cannot establish their identity or activity, and therapeutic heterogeneity across cholesterol-dependent tumor phenotypes. Biomaterials that target cholesterol metabolism offer a promising route to overcome therapy resistance and improve combination immunotherapy, but their clinical translation will require precise definition of responsive tumor types, target cell populations and actionable metabolic vulnerabilities.

title: Wireless bioelectronic stimulation enhanced by electroconductive silk bioink modulates human iPSC-cardiomyocyte contractility and structural organisation
abstract: Bioelectronic interfaces can support cardiac cell function after myocardial injury by restoring disrupted electrical signalling, while enabling controlled electrical stimulation (ES). Here, we develop a pH-regulated silk fibroin/glycidoxy-silane stabilised poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):poly(styrene sulfonate) (SF/PP) bioink formulation for extrusion-printable cardiac bioelectronic interfaces. Specifically, pH neutralisation during blending moderates rapid SF-PP interactions, delays premature gelation and enables homogeneous extrusion printing. The optimised SF/PP formulations exhibit shear-thinning behaviour, continuous filament formation and stable printed grid geometries, while PP incorporation regulates hydrogel microstructure, swelling behaviour, mechanics and electrical impedance. The SF/PP bioink formulations support human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived cardiomyocyte (hiCM) viability and enabled cell-laden printing of hiPSC-derived cardiac fibroblasts (hiCFs) into tubular and grid constructs with post-printing viability. When used as conductive hydrogel interfaces for capacitive-coupling wireless electrical stimulation (WES), the SF/PP formulations enhanced cardiomyocyte contraction amplitude, calcium signal propagation and sarcomeric organisation. The higher PEDOT formulation promotes more coordinated calcium propagation, while WES increases sarcomere length and is associated with higher Cx43 puncta density. These findings establish pH-regulated SF/PP bioinks as printable cardiac bioelectronic interfaces for wireless bioelectronic conditioning of human iPSC-derived cardiac cell constructs, supporting future development of electrically functional platforms for post-infarct cardiac repair studies.

title: Multifunctional cascade nanosystem consumes glucose to trigger enhanced pyroptosis and cuproptosis for tumor immunotherapy
abstract: Immunogenic cell death (ICD) bridged local therapy and systemic immune activation by releasing damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) that provoked antitumor responses. Pyroptosis, a pro-inflammatory cell death mode, induced local tumor demise and releases cytokines that facilitated immune activation. In this study, we constructed a multifunctional cascade nanosystem CaO 2 /Cu-ZIF8/GOX (CaO 2 /CZ/GOX) that triggered mitochondrial oxidative stress through glucose consumption and ion homeostasis disturbance and cuproptosis, thereby amplifying tumor pyroptosis. The nanosystem utilized acid-responsive Cu-ZIF8 (CZ) as a carrier to load CaO 2 and glucose oxidase (GOX). In the acidic tumor microenvironment (TME), CaO 2 initiated cascaded H 2 O 2 generation, while GOX concurrently consumed glucose and catalytically generated H 2 O 2 , synergistically exacerbating ion homeostasis disruption and mitochondrial oxidative stress. Meanwhile, Cu 2+ released from Cu-ZIF8 participated in Fenton-like reactions to generate hydroxyl radicals (·OH), and accumulated Cu 2+ further triggered FDX1-mediated cuproptosis. Collectively, these events resulted in reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, ion homeostasis disruption, and mitochondrial damage, ultimately activating tumor cell pyroptosis and cuproptosis. In vitro and in vivo assays confirmed that CaO 2 /CZ/GOX NPs efficiently consumed glucose, selectively accumulated in tumor, and exhibited favorable biocompatibility. Moreover, they significantly inhibited Hepa1-6 tumor cell proliferation, effectively suppressed tumor recurrence and activated antitumor immunity. Overall, this nanosystem integrated a cascade of metabolic intervention, oxidative damage, cuproptosis, pyroptosis, and immune activation, offering a new strategy for tumor metabolic regulation and immune microenvironment remodeling.

title: Bio-dissociable platinum quantum dot cluster nanozymes for nonhormonal endometriosis therapy through microenvironment remodeling
abstract: Endometriosis (EMS) is a chronic inflammatory disorder marked by ectopic endometrial lesions that commonly cause pain and infertility. Existing surgical and hormonal therapies are limited by adverse effects and high recurrence rates, while nanozyme-based approaches offer opportunities to develop alternative therapeutic strategies. Here, we developed bio-dissociable platinum quantum dot clusters (PtQDC) as nanozymes for nonhormonal EMS therapy. PtQDC undergoes gradual dissociation in lesion tissue fluid and exhibits sustained scavenging activity toward reactive oxygen and nitrogen species. The resulting shift of endometriotic cells from their highly oxidative state beyond a favorable redox window was accompanied by impaired energy metabolism, mitochondrial dysfunction, and apoptosis. In the mouse model of EMS, PtQDC reduced lesion number and volume, remodeled the peritoneal microenvironment, inhibited pathological angiogenesis, and attenuated pain-associated signaling. PtQDC also reduced proinflammatory factors, increased IL-10, and modulated macrophage phenotypic profiles. RNA-seq analysis further revealed downregulation of Ptgs2, Mmp3, and Postn, genes associated with inflammation, invasion, and fibrosis. Thus, PtQDC integrates antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antifibrotic, and antiangiogenic activities as a potential multitarget nonhormonal therapy for EMS.

title: Ocular delivery of repurposed everolimus against dry eye with a tear-triggered in situ hydrogel based on enhanced solubilization and retention
abstract: ABSTRACT Dry eye represents an increasingly prominent public health burden in modern society. However, the limitations of currently available treatment options have necessitated the pursuit of new therapies. Here we report the repurposing of everolimus (Evero), an mTOR inhibitor with poor aqueous solubility, for dry eye management. Meanwhile, a tear-triggered in situ gelling system (EveroGel) based on the design principle of enhanced solubilization and retention was developed for topical administration of Evero. It was showed that the proposed formulation strategy can facilitate tissue permeation and decrease lacrimal clearance. Evero mitigated the severity of dry eye in a scopolamine-induced mouse model regarding corneal fluorescein, TUNEL, K10 immunofluorescent and conjunctival PAS staining. However, more favorable outcomes were obtained with EveroGel. All excipients present in EveroGel are FDA-approved. Hence, no toxic effects have been observed in the in vivo biocompatibility study. Our work demonstrates the therapeutic potential of rationally engineered ophthalmic formulations of Evero for treating dry eye.

title: Naringenin-Mn self-fueling dual-dynamic hydrogel with cascade catalysis and immunomodulation properties for repairing MRSA-infected diabetic wounds
abstract: Chronic infectious wounds in diabetic patients remain a significant clinical challenge due to persistent inflammation, oxidative stress, and bacterial resistance issues. This problem is particularly acute in the area of postoperative surgical incisions, where impaired healing can lead to serious complications. This study aimed to develop a self-healing cascade-catalyzed hydrogel, CS-PBA/ODex@NRGe-Mn (CPONM), featuring borate and Schiff base bonds. This hydrogel exhibits a dual dynamic network structure and incorporates naringenin-Mn nanoparticles (NM NPs) with SOD/POD-like activity. The hydrogel was synthesized by mixing CS-PBA solution with ODex solution containing NM NPs. CPONM exhibits high porosity, swelling capacity, adhesion strength (13.43 kPa), and pH-responsive release properties. In vitro studies demonstrated that CPONM effectively inhibited the growth of Escherichia coli (E.coli, 93.15%) and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA, 94.74%), disrupted bacterial biofilms by up to 92%, and reduced iNOS and IL-6 expression in macrophages. In a diabetic mouse wound model infected with MRSA, CPONM accelerated wound healing (reaching 97.47% by day 18), reduced bacterial infection risk, inhibited NF-κB, and activated Nrf2. Histopathological staining revealed the hydrogel's ability to promote wound epithelialization, collagen deposition, and vascular growth (VEGF, α-SMA). Therefore, CPONM represents a promising approach for treating infected postoperative wounds in diabetic patients.

title: Robust optical metasurface heterostructures for prevention and treatment of peri-implantitis
abstract: Peri-implantitis poses significant challenges in the field of oral implantology, while the inherent antibacterial properties of implant abutments and their tight sealing with surrounding soft tissues play a vital role in the prevent and treatment of peri-implantitis. Herein, a robust optical metasurface CeO x /TiO 2 heterostructure with gradient-distributed nanocavity structure was prepared on titanium surface by innovatively integrating plasma immersion ion implantation and thermal treatment technologies. The CeO x /TiO 2 heterostructure with an optimized bandgap enhances light absorption in the second near-infrared region and a robust optical metasurface with gradient-distributed nanocavities improves the retention of NIR light by the light trap effect and increases the heat preservation capacity, leading to superior photothermal antibacterial activity in vitro and in vivo . Besides, with the existence of ceria, metasurface CeO x /TiO 2 heterostructure shows antioxidant properties and can alleviate the local inflammatory microenvironment, promoting soft tissue sealing in vitro and in vivo by sequentially activating the “Neuroactive ligand-receptor interaction, Rap1 signaling pathway, and ECM-receptor interaction” cascade network . This study paves the way for developing novel dental implant abutments with antibacterial activities and soft tissue sealing properties based on optical metasurface heterostructures for prevention and treatment of peri-implantitis.

title: TRPA1 blockade potentiates a ferroptosis-driven in situ vaccine nanoplatform for enhanced ROS immunotherapy against TNBC
abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) treatment is constrained by chemotherapy resistance and poor immunotherapy responses. ROS-based therapies, including sonodynamic therapy (SDT) and chemodynamic therapy (CDT), hold promise but are limited by intrinsic antioxidant defenses of tumor cells. TRPA1, a redox-sensitive calcium channel, serves as a critical rheostat in the oxidative defense program of TNBC cells. By sustaining calcium influx, TRPA1 buffers oxidative stress and dampens ROS-mediated killing, thereby enhancing resistance to ROS-based therapies. TRPA1 blockade represents a promising strategy to both sensitize tumor cells to oxidative damage and amplify the immunogenic effects triggered by SDT/CDT. Here, we incorporated this TRPA1 blockade strategy into a FeMOF-based nanoplatform (FMHG-HA) that co-delivers glucose oxidase (GOx) and HC-030031, with hyaluronic acid (HA) for tumor-associated delivery. GOx depletes glucose and generates H 2 O 2 in situ to fuel Fenton-like reactions for self-powered CDT. Ultrasound (US) further amplifies ROS production, synergizing with CDT to drive lipid peroxidation and GPX4 downregulation. Meanwhile, HC-030031 abrogates TRPA1-mediated calcium influx, eliminating the tolerance buffer and shifting the cell death modality from apoptosis to ferroptosis. In orthotopic 4T1 models, FMHG-HA-mediated CDT/SDT, upon US irradiation, substantially inhibited tumor progression and reduced pulmonary metastasis. Notably, ferroptosis released DAMPs that converted dying tumor cells into an individualized antigen depot, eliciting an in situ vaccine-like immune activation, promoting dendritic cell maturation and CD8 + T cell infiltration, effectively turning immunologically “cold” tumors “hot”. Collectively, FMHG-HA couples TRPA1-targeted ion intervention with multimodal oxidative therapy, representing a strategy that uses ferroptosis as the engine and in situ vaccine-like immune activation as the functional output for TNBC treatment.

title: Injectable self-healing hydrogel delivering trispecific engineered exosomes for osteoporotic bone regeneration via activating mitophagy
abstract: Osteoporotic bone defects are characterized by impaired matrix remodeling, diminished osteogenic potential, and insufficient vascularization, posing major challenges for tissue regeneration. Mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomes (MSCs-Exos) have shown promise in promoting osteogenesis and angiogenesis, but their clinical translation is limited by rapid clearance and lack of targeted delivery. Here, we report the development of an injectable, self-healing SK/HA@A hydrogel for sustained delivery of trispecific RNA-engineered exosomes (Tri-Exos) targeting IL31, CELA1, and PCOLCE2. Tri-Exos were engineered via electroporation and rigorously characterized for morphology, size, marker expression, cellular uptake, and functional regulation of target genes in BMSCs. The hydrogel exhibited rapid gelation, robust mechanical properties, dynamic self-healing, and sustained release of Tri-Exos over 30 days. In vitro, SK/HA@A@EVs significantly enhanced BMSC osteogenic differentiation, matrix mineralization, and HUVEC angiogenic responses, while simultaneously activating mitophagy-mediated mitochondrial regulation and autophagy-associated survival pathways, which are critical for maintaining cellular homeostasis under osteoporotic conditions. In a rat femoral defect model, hydrogel treatment improved bone volume, mineral density, and vascularization, as confirmed by micro-CT, histological analyses, and gene expression profiling. Collectively, these results demonstrate that the SK/HA@A@EVs platform orchestrates osteoporotic bone regeneration through synergistic modulation of osteogenesis, angiogenesis, and mitophagy-driven cellular survival pathways. This study provides a translational strategy integrating engineered exosomes with functional hydrogels for targeted, localized therapy of osteoporotic bone defects.

title: Sequential blood-brain barrier-penetrating and microglial-mitochondria-targeting nanosystem for ischemic stroke therapy
abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) causes severe neurological deficits closely linked to microglial overactivation after ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury, a process governed by mitochondrial homeostasis. However, restoring microglial mitochondrial function across the blood–brain barrier (BBB) remains challenging. Here, we report a sequentially targeted nanosystem, M-BPM@TGPB, for I/R injury therapy. It comprises a triphenylphosphonium (TPP)-modified, gadolinium-doped Prussian blue core and a mannose-modified BV2–platelet hybrid membrane shell. This design integrates mannose for BBB penetration, platelet membrane for lesion targeting, BV2 membrane for microglial uptake, and TPP for mitochondrial localization, enabling precise vascular-to-subcellular delivery. In vitro, the nanosystem crossed the BBB, localized to BV2 mitochondria, scavenged reactive oxygen species (ROS), restored mitochondrial function, and inhibited inflammation. In a mouse model of middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R), the intravenously administered nanosystem accumulated in microglial mitochondria, scavenged mitochondrial ROS (mtROS), restored mitochondrial homeostasis, promoted M1-to-M2 polarization, suppressed neuroinflammation, reduced neuronal apoptosis, and promoted angiogenesis, thereby reducing infarct volume from 36.61% to 10.57% and the modified neurological severity score (mNSS) from 14 to 2.5. It also exhibited favorable biocompatibility and enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) contrast. Critically, rather than broadly scavenging ROS, this strategy specifically restores microglial mitochondrial function, shifting the therapeutic focus from general antioxidant approaches to organelle-specific intervention. This work may offer a promising design paradigm for nanotherapies targeting central nervous system disorders in which mitochondrial dysfunction and neuroinflammation are core pathological drivers.

title: Developing precision nanoparticle-based drug delivery systems for Alzheimer's disease therapy
abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is an irreversible neurodegenerative disease that has thus far suffered from unsatisfactory therapeutic outcomes. Despite ongoing research into AD pathogenesis and related drugs, few disease-modifying therapies are currently available. Moreover, efficient drug delivery is significantly hindered by low permeability of the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and non-specific distribution within the brain, further limiting the efficacy of existing anti-AD medications. Nanotechnology has recently emerged as a promising approach to overcome these challenges. This review aims to offer a comprehensive overview of recent advances in precision nanoparticle-based drug delivery systems for AD therapy. First, we outline the multiple pathological mechanisms and representative pathogenesis-inspired therapies of AD. Next, we summarize various types of nanoparticles that have been utilized in AD drug delivery, including polymeric, lipid-based, inorganic, and biomimetic nanocarriers. Subsequently, we highlight the nanoparticle-mediated strategies for cascaded precision drug delivery at different levels, focusing on both the BBB and specific pathologies or cell populations within AD lesions. Finally, we discuss potential challenges and prospects in employing precision delivery systems, aiming to accelerate the development and clinical translation of nanoparticle-based therapies for AD.

title: Sono-enzymatically engineered tannic acid/doxycycline-lignin nanoparticles enable self-assembled bioactive chitosan hydrogels for chronic wound healing
abstract: Chronic wounds remain a major clinical challenge due to their multifactorial pathology, characterised by excessive proteolytic and oxidative enzyme activity, persistent inflammation, bacterial infection, and biofilm formation. Here, we report a green, nano-enabled hydrogel fabricated through the in situ self-assembly of thiolated chitosan (TCS), driven by tannic acid/doxycycline-functionalised lignin nanoparticles (PLD NPs). Doxycycline was incorporated at a sub-inhibitory concentration (12.5 μg/mL), enabling PLD NPs (0.5 mg/mL) to inhibit matrix metalloproteinase (MMP) activity by approximately 50% without inducing antibacterial effects. Dynamic interactions between the polymer network and NPs produced injectable, self-healing hydrogels capable of stimuli-responsive NPs release under chronic wound-like conditions, including variations in pH, hydrogen peroxide, and lysozyme. Ex vivo evaluation using human chronic wound exudates demonstrated potent inhibition of MMP and myeloperoxidase activities by 73% and 80%, respectively. The hydrogels further exhibited strong antimicrobial and antibiofilm activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa , achieving 4.8- and 4.3-log reductions in bacterial viability while preventing 73% and 65% of biofilm formation, respectively. In vitro studies confirmed excellent biocompatibility with human keratinocytes and fibroblasts, together with up to 82% cellular antioxidant activity and enhanced fibroblast migration. Importantly, in an in vivo full-thickness S. aureus -infected mouse wound model, the hydrogels achieved complete wound closure within 18 days, outperforming commercial antiseptic treatments. Overall, this work demonstrates a multifunctional hydrogel platform that simultaneously modulates the chronic wound microenvironment, controls infection and biofilm formation, reduces oxidative stress, and promotes tissue regeneration, offering a promising strategy for advanced chronic wound management.

title: Progress and applications of microneedle-based gene therapy
abstract: : Gene therapy holds considerable promise for treating a wide range of intractable diseases through the modification of specific genes. However, gene therapeutics such as plasmid DNA, messenger RNA, and CRISPR-based systems are susceptible to degradation, face challenges in crossing cellular barriers, and may induce immune-related adverse effects, thereby limiting their clinical translation. Microneedles create microchannels that penetrate tissue barriers and, when combined with various carrier materials, enhance nucleic acid stability and intracellular delivery efficiency. This review summarizes the compatibility of different microneedle configurations with gene-delivery vectors, compares the effects of various fabrication processes on the activity of therapeutic agents, and elucidates the mechanisms underlying barrier penetration and delivery by microneedles. Recent advances in the application of microneedle-based gene therapy in dermatology, oncology, and nucleic acid vaccination are also discussed.
