Finally, current challenges, including drug loading, mass production, and safety evaluation, are analyzed, and the prospects for smart, responsive, and integrated diagnostic and therapeutic microneedles are highlighted.

title: Injectable Thermoresponsive Hydrogel Integrating pH-Responsive Nanoparticles for Antioxidant Therapy of Intervertebral Disc Degeneration
abstract: : Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) is one of the leading causes of low back pain and spinal dysfunction, severely impairing patients’ quality of life and imposing a substantial societal burden. However, effective therapeutic strategies capable of fundamentally slowing or delaying disease progression remain lacking. Given the central role of oxidative stress in IVDD progression, the development of therapies with both antioxidant capacity and multi-target regulatory effects is of considerable importance. Previous studies have demonstrated that epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) and metformin (MET) exert synergistic antioxidant and cytoprotective effects; however, their clinical application is limited by the low bioavailability of EGCG and the relatively weak antioxidant capacity of MET.In this study, EGCG–MET self-assembled polyphenolic nanoparticles (EMNP) were constructed via a Mannich reaction to enable synergistic delivery and functional enhancement of both agents. This nanosystem exhibits pH-responsive dissociation under acidic microenvironmental conditions, thereby facilitating on-demand drug release. Furthermore, EMNP were incorporated into a thermosensitive hydrogel composed of poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) (PNIPAAm) and polyvinyl alcohol (PVA), fabricated via in situ free-radical polymerization (PNIPAAm–PVA hydrogel), to form an injectable, in situ gelling composite delivery system (TPP@EMNP). The phase-transition behavior of PNIPAAm enabled rapid gelation in vivo, while PVA enhanced mechanical stability and local retention.In an IVDD model, TPP@EMNP effectively scavenged reactive oxygen species, thereby attenuating degenerative processes at multiple levels. This strategy integrates pH-responsive self-assembled nanoparticles with a thermosensitive hydrogel-based delivery platform, offering a promising approach with potential clinical translational value for minimally invasive treatment of IVDD.

title: "Threefold dual" copper homeostasis regulation strategy: Targeted copper surge for enhanced cancer immunotherapy
abstract: ABSTRACT Copper-based therapeutics disrupting intracellular copper homeostasis hold immense promise for cancer immunotherapy, yet their efficacy is severely limited by inadequate copper accumulation, intratumoral antioxidant defenses, and nonspecific drug release. To surmount these limitations, we engineered CuTF-DC_AC50, an innovative copper homeostasis nanomodulator implementing a "threefold dual" strategy to maximize therapeutic outcomes. Specifically, the nanomodulator drives massive copper overload through a dual-channel influx and efflux regulation mechanism, concurrently delivering exogenous Cu 2+ and inhibiting ATOX1-mediated copper efflux via its DC_AC50 component. Simultaneously, it dismantles the intracellular antioxidant barrier through dual-mechanism glutathione (GSH) depletion, mediated by disulfide bond cleavage within the TPH scaffold alongside Cu 2+ reduction. Furthermore, CuTF-DC_AC50 undergoes dual-responsive degradation triggered by the acidic and GSH-abundant tumor microenvironment (TME), enabling precise drug release and spatial-temporal orchestration of the therapeutic cascade. This targeted copper surge synergistically triggers cuproptosis and pyroptosis, thereby robustly activating immunogenic cell death (ICD). Consequently, in vivo investigations demonstrate that this nanomodulator profoundly remodels the immunosuppressive TME, promotes robust immune cell infiltration, and substantially suppresses tumor growth. By exploiting the CuTF-DC_AC50-induced PD-L1 upregulation, its combination with αPD-L1 markedly amplifies therapeutic efficacy in CT26 tumor-bearing mice, establishing a highly programmable and clinically translatable combinatorial strategy for potentiated cancer immunotherapy.

title: Restorative endothelium and polarization-assisted inflammatory regulation nanomedicine (REPAIR) for acute lung injury treatment
abstract: ABSTRACT Acute lung injury (ALI) is marked by uncontrolled inflammation and excessive immune cell infiltration, ultimately causing endothelial barrier disruption and impaired pulmonary function. To counteract these pathological processes, we develop a Restorative Endothelium and Polarization-Assisted Inflammatory Regulation nanomedicine (REPAIR) that integrates endothelial protection with alveolar macrophage reprogramming. REPAIR is fabricated by loading the P2X7 receptor‌ (P2X7R) antagonist A740003 into apoptotic NIH3T3 cell vesicles (Apo-Vesicles), thereby combining apoptotic cell-derived “eat-me” signals with targeted inhibition of P2X7R-mediated inflammatory pathways. Benefiting from its apoptotic cell-mimetic surface, REPAIR exhibits markedly enhanced uptake by alveolar macrophages (AMs), driving the transition of pro-inflammatory M1 macrophages toward an anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype. At the same time, the released A740003 efficiently suppresses P2X7R activation, preventing macrophage necrosis and preserving endothelial vascular endothelial (VE)-cadherin to maintain vascular barrier integrity. In vitro and in vivo studies further confirm that REPAIR substantially reduces inflammatory cytokine production, limits macrophage necrosis, and stabilizes endothelial junctions through the synergistic interplay of apoptotic mimicry and P2X7R antagonism. These results highlight REPAIR as a promising and mechanistically comprehensive nanotherapeutic strategy for ALI and other inflammation-driven pulmonary diseases.

title: Corrigendum to “A biomimetic chondrocyte membrane-camouflaged tFNA nanoplatform for reprogramming the cartilage–synovium axis in osteoarthritis” [Mater. Today Bio 40, October 2026, 103609]
Adhesive hydrogel-mediated spatiotemporal delivery of garlic-derived nanovesicles reprograms immunometabolism to rescue periodontal bone regeneration
abstract: The core challenge in regenerating inflammatory bone defects, such as periodontitis-related bone resorption, lies in the dysregulation of the immune-metabolic microenvironment, which required implanted materials to simultaneously possess tissue sealing properties, sustained immune modulation capacity and metabolic intervention functions. Herein, garlic-derived exosome-like nanovesicles (GaELNs), exhibiting anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory activities, are embedded in an injectable, tissue-adhesive polyethylene glycol hydrogel (GaE-PEG) to meet the challenges. The hydrogel exhibited favorable tissue adhesion and sustained release of GaELN-associated protein in vitro . GaE-PEG promoted macrophage polarization toward an anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype and reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine expression. In lipopolysaccharide-stimulated periodontal ligament stem cells, GaE-PEG alleviated mitochondrial oxidative stress, restored oxidative phosphorylation, suppressed excessive glycolysis, and enhanced osteogenic differentiation. Transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses linked these effects to mitochondrial metabolic regulation, while oligomycin treatment attenuated the osteogenic response, supporting a contribution of oxidative phosphorylation. In a rat model of periodontitis-related bone defects, GaE-PEG reduced local inflammation and promoted alveolar bone regeneration, with improved regenerative outcomes compared with a single local injection of free GaELNs at an equivalent dose and Bio-Gide™/Bio-Oss™ treatment. These findings support an adhesive hydrogel strategy integrating local nanovesicle delivery with immunomodulation and metabolic regulation to promote bone regeneration under inflammatory conditions.

title: Biomimetic Hf-MOF/Mn3O4 STING nanoagonist potentiates radio-immunotherapy by remodeling tumor microenvironment and activating cGAS-STING pathway
abstract: Tumor hypoxia and immunosuppression not only drive radioresistance in cancer radiotherapy but also compromise the efficacy of immunotherapy. Here, a biomimetic core–shell nanoagonist (CM/HPM) integrating a radiosensitizing hafnium-based metal-organic framework (Hf-MOF) core with a tumor microenvironment (TME)-responsive Mn 3 O 4 shell is reported to orchestrate robust radio-immunotherapy. The Hf-MOF core serves as a powerful radiosensitizer, enhancing localized radiation energy deposition and amplifying radiation-induced DNA damage. The Mn 3 O 4 shell exhibits multienzyme-mimicking activities, catalyzing oxygen generation to relieve hypoxia, depleting glutathione to amplify oxidative stress, and releasing Mn 2+ ions upon TME-triggered degradation. The liberated Mn 2+ acts as a critical immune co-agonist, sensitizing cyclic GMP-AMP synthase (cGAS) to cytosolic DNA fragments from Hf-MOF-enhanced radiotherapy, thereby synergistically activating the cGAS-STING pathway. Moreover, the cancer-cell-membrane coating enables homologous targeting and facilitates uptake by both tumor cells and immune cells. In bilateral 4T1 tumor-bearing mice, CM/HPM combined with X-ray irradiation ablates primary tumors and evokes a potent abscopal effect, suppressing distant tumors via enhanced intratumoral T-cell infiltration and dendritic cell (DC) maturation. This synergistic nanoplatform overcomes radioresistance and elicits systemic antitumor immunity, offering a promising paradigm for metastatic cancer therapy.

title: A pH-responsive GelMA-KerMA hydrogel delivering luteolin-loaded PLGA nanoparticles promotes myocardial repair via Akt/Bad signaling and multitarget regulation
abstract: Myocardial infarction (MI) triggers cardiomyocyte apoptosis, oxidative stress imbalance, ventricular fibrosis, and impaired angiogenesis. Luteolin, a natural flavonoid compound, possesses antioxidant, anti-apoptotic, and cardioprotective properties, making it a promising candidate for MI treatment. However, its poor water solubility, low bioavailability, and chemical instability severely hinder its clinical translation. To address these limitations, we developed a photo-crosslinked composite hydrogel delivery system using gelatin methacryloyl and keratin methacryloyl (GelMA-KerMA). Luteolin-loaded poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) nanoparticles were uniformly dispersed within a three-dimensional gel network to achieve pH-triggered local drug delivery. The covalent GelMA–KerMA network retained structural integrity under both pH conditions. In the weakly acidic infarct microenvironment, acid-catalyzed hydrolysis of PLGA ester bonds was the primary driver of accelerated luteolin release, whereas the network mainly acted as a sustained-retarding reservoir. The incorporation of KerMA endowed the patch with enhanced mechanical stability and cytocompatibility, enabling better mechanical matching with the infarcted myocardium. The composite hydrogel promotes myocardial repair and functional recovery through the coordinated regulation of the rapid Akt/Bad phosphorylation cascade. It also sustains MAPK/Rap1-dependent transcriptional reprogramming. It inhibits mitochondrial apoptosis, scavenges reactive oxygen species (ROS), suppresses fibroblast activation, and promotes neovascularization. This study presents a protein-based delivery platform that integrates tailored physicochemical and mechanical properties with multi-pathway myocardial repair capabilities, offering a biomaterial strategy for minimally invasive local drug delivery in ischemic MI.

title: Reprogrammed macrophage-derived nanovesicle–lipid nanoparticle hybrids for cardiac siRUNX1 delivery: Therapeutic evaluation in Ang II-induced cardiac remodeling
abstract: Targeted delivery of small interfering RNA (siRNA) to the heart remains challenging because conventional lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) predominantly accumulate in the liver following systemic administration. To improve cardiac siRNA delivery, we developed a biomimetic hybrid nanoplatform by co-extruding siRUNX1-loaded LNPs with reprogrammed macrophage-derived nanovesicles (rMNVs) obtained from sequentially LPS/TGF-β1-treated RAW264.7 macrophages, followed by surface functionalization with a cardiac-targeting peptide (CTP). The sequentially treated donor cells exhibited a phenotypic shift characterized by reduced M1-associated markers and enhanced M2-associated features. The resulting CTP-hLNPs maintained a nanoscale spherical morphology, high siRNA encapsulation efficiency, and retained donor-cell-derived membrane components, including CD206. In vitro, CTP-hLNPs showed reduced uptake by RAW264.7 macrophages while maintaining cellular internalization and siRUNX1 activity in H9c2 cardiac-derived cells. Following intravenous administration, CTP-hLNPs exhibited reduced liver-associated fluorescence and increased heart-associated fluorescence at 24 h compared with conventional CTP-LNPs. Therapeutic efficacy was subsequently evaluated in an angiotensin II (Ang II)-induced mouse model of cardiac remodeling. CTP-hLNP@siRUNX1 reduced cardiac RUNX1 mRNA expression and improved left ventricular systolic function, as indicated by increased left ventricular ejection fraction and fractional shortening. Treatment also attenuated cardiac hypertrophic remodeling, including reductions in the heart weight-to-body weight ratio and cardiomyocyte cross-sectional area. In addition, CTP-hLNP@siRUNX1 reduced myofibroblast-associated α-SMA expression, collagen deposition, and myocardial fibrotic area. Collectively, these findings support rMNV–LNP hybridization combined with CTP functionalization as a potential delivery strategy for cardiac RNA interference therapy and demonstrate its therapeutic effects in Ang II-induced cardiac remodeling.

title: Dual-action nanotheranostics targeting cell-free DNA rescues aberrant alternative polyadenylation to ameliorate periodontitis
abstract: While periodontal pathogens (Porphyromonas gingivalis) are known to severely disrupt macrophage post-transcriptional homeostasis, the precise extracellular instigator remains elusive. Here, through comparative transcriptomic profiling, we identify cell-free DNA (cfDNA) as this fundamental pathogenic trigger. Comprehensive bioinformatic analysis uncovers that cfDNA governs macrophage fate by fundamentally rewiring the global alternative polyadenylation (APA) equilibrium. Specifically, cfDNA forces pro-inflammatory (M1) transcripts into translationally hyperactive short-3'-untranslated region (3'UTR) isoforms, while simultaneously suppressing anti-inflammatory (M2) programs via 3'UTR lengthening. To therapeutically intercept this cfDNA-APA pathogenic axis, we engineered a homologous nanotheranostic platform (DA-APAT). Addressing the unique clinical demands for early periodontitis screening, its polycationic PEI shell enables highly sensitive salivary cfDNA theranostic monitoring. Crucially, this monitoring readout directly calibrates the in situ enzymatic clearance load executed by the internally encapsulated DNase I. Synergized by the intrinsic reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging capability of the hollow mesoporous cerium oxide core, this monitoring nanoplatform decisively silences intracellular DNA-sensing pathways (cGAS-STING/TLR9), rectifies the disrupted APA, and contributes robust M2 macrophage repolarization. In an orthotopic murine periodontitis model, this nanotherapy effectively halts alveolar bone loss and facilitates profound periodontal regeneration with excellent biocompatibility. This work unveils a cfDNA-driven RNA regulatory paradigm in immune dysregulation and provides a monitoring precision nanotheranostic modality for inflammatory therapy.

title: Scaffold-free self-assembled cell ring organoids enable efficient tumor modeling with high engraftment rates, superior tumor uniformity, and reduced animal consumption
abstract: Background Conventional tumor cell suspension xenografts suffer from low engraftment efficiency, prolonged latency, and poor tumor uniformity, with high animal consumption conflicting with the 3R principles (Replacement, Reduction, Refinement). This study aimed to develop a scaffold-free self-assembled cell ring organoid platform to address these bottlenecks. Methods Tumor cells and fibroblasts were mixed at optimized ratios and seeded into microwell molds, spontaneously self-assembling into ring-shaped organoids within 24–48 h without exogenous matrices or hydrogels. In vitro characterization included live/dead staining, histology, immunofluorescence, flow cytometry, Western blotting, and transcriptomic sequencing. In vivo performance was evaluated by orthotopic transplantation into the lateral femoral condyle of immunodeficient or immunocompetent mice, with longitudinal monitoring by bioluminescence imaging and micro-CT. Results Cell rings maintained high viability during in vitro culture and were compatible with both cell lines and clinical primary sarcoma cells. Immunofluorescence and Western blotting revealed that co-cultured fibroblasts underwent cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF)-like phenotypic transformation (α-SMA upregulation) within the cell ring organoids. Transcriptomic analysis further demonstrated that the gene expression profiles of cell ring organoids closely resembled those of original tumors, whereas 2D-cultured cells showed the greatest number and magnitude of differentially expressed genes. In vivo , cell ring organoids achieved higher engraftment rates, better tumor uniformity, and stronger bone invasion capacity compared with cell suspensions. Conclusion The scaffold-free self-assembled cell ring organoids platform provides an efficient, uniform, and 3R-compliant strategy for animal tumor modeling. Without requiring exogenous matrices, this technology achieves significantly higher engraftment rates and tumor uniformity compared with conventional methods, effectively reduces animal consumption, and may offer a potential platform for future preclinical drug screening and tumor microenvironment (TME) research.

title: Multifunctional bio-derived hydrogel loaded with ADSCs for promoting diabetic wound healing
abstract: Adipose-derived stem cells (ADSCs) hold substantial therapeutic potential for diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs). However, their efficacy is often limited by poor survival within the harsh microenvironment of chronic wounds. In this study, we developed a multifunctional bio-derived hydrogel composed of gelatin methacrylate (GelMA), glycyrrhizic acid (GA), and ferrous ions (Fe 2+ ) that integrates ADSCs with local microenvironment modulation. This approach targets key pathological challenges in DFUs treatment, including persistent inflammation, impaired angiogenesis, and oxidative stress. The hydrogel demonstrated potent antibacterial, antioxidant, and pro-angiogenic activities. Moreover, it significantly accelerated diabetic wound healing, enhanced re-epithelialization and collagen deposition, and promoted macrophage polarization toward the reparative M2 phenotype, thereby effectively improving the wound microenvironment. These results indicate that the GelMA/GA/Fe@ADSCs hydrogel is a promising regenerative therapy with strong translational potential for DFUs and other chronic wounds.

title: Human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cell-derived small extracellular vesicles delivering CERS1 promote squamous differentiation in HPV16-positive cervical intraepithelial neoplasia via remodeling sphingomyelin metabolism
abstract: Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN), a precursor of human papillomavirus (HPV)-driven cervical cancer, poses a severe threat to women’s health. High-risk HPV infection drives CIN progression, whereas well-defined intervention targets and effective non-invasive therapies remain lacking. Herein, Using New Approach Methodologies (NAMs), specifically HPV16-positive ectocervical organoids as a human-relevant disease model, we evaluated the therapeutic potential of engineered cell-free small extracellular vesicles derived from human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells (hucMSC-sEV). We found that hucMSC-sEV significantly promoted squamous differentiation in S12 cells and HPV16-positive ectocervical organoids. Mechanistically, integrated multi-omics analyses within this NAMs platform revealed that hucMSC-sEV delivered ceramide synthase 1 (CERS1) to upregulate C18 ceramide (C18 Cer) synthesis, activating the non-canonical p53 signaling to drive squamous differentiation. In NCG mice bearing subcutaneous xenografts of S12 cells, hucMSC-sEV effectively inhibited S12 xenograft growth and modulated squamous differentiation via regulation of C18 ceramide metabolism, while this therapeutic effect was abrogated in CERS1-knockdown hucMSC-sEV. This study delineates the molecular mechanism by which hucMSC-sEV remodel sphingolipid metabolism to promote cervical squamous epithelial differentiation and suppress S12 xenograft development, providing novel potential targets and therapeutic strategies for CIN intervention.

title: Brain-penetrating and lesion-triggered hydrogen sulfide nanocarrier for multiple pathogenic interventions in Parkinson's disease therapy
abstract: : The defective hydrogen sulfide (H 2 S) metabolism in brain has emerged as a crucial pathogenic event and therapeutic target in Parkinson's disease (PD). However, current H 2 S delivery approaches for PD remain predominantly limited by the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and on-demand supply. This work aimed to upgrade the delivery of H 2 S to across BBB, thereby adequately harnessing its neuroprotective effect in PD brain. We developed a reactive oxygen species (ROS)-triggered H 2 S nanocarrier with brain-penetrating capability (RVG29/TK@Lip/GYY) for targeted H 2 S delivery in PD brain. In this system, the H 2 S donor GYY4137 was assembled by a ROS-responsive thioketal linker (TK), while the surface is modified with the brain-homing peptide RVG29. Notably, this formulation achieved a good BBB penetration rate of 22.1%. In addition, pathological evaluation results demonstrated that the controlled H 2 S release by RVG29/TK@Lip/GYY can exert multiple PD pathogenic interventions, including scavenging excessive ROS, alleviating nitrative stress, decreasing nerve cells apoptosis, reducing glial cell activation and promoting nerve regeneration. Critically, RVG29/TK@Lip/GYY treatment significantly attenuated the motor deficits of PD model mice. Collectively, this study not only provide a H 2 S-nanocarrier for PD multiple pathological therapy, but also contributing to the development of H 2 S delivery in other neurodegenerative diseases treatment.

title: A multifunctional QK@ZIF-8@GA hydrogel promotes vascularized bone regeneration in diabetic bone defects by remodeling the osteoimmune microenvironment
Gene-Activated Matrices as Nanomedicine Platforms for Bone Regeneration: Delivery, Translation and Patent Landscape
abstract: Protein biologics are constrained in critical-size bone defects not by insufficient potency, but by rapid clearance and the inability to sustain therapeutic signaling at the repair site. Dose escalation does not overcome this pharmacokinetic limitation and instead increases the risk of ectopic bone formation, osteolysis, and soft tissue toxicity. Sustained, localized delivery, not higher dosing, is the unmet requirement. Gene-activated matrices (GAM) address this problem by integrating nucleic acid cargo and delivery vectors within an implantable scaffold, converting infiltrating host cells into local sources of regenerative signals. This review examines GAMs as nanomedicine platforms for bone regeneration, tracing their development from scaffold bioactivity and the limitation of protein biologics to nucleic acid-based delivery. We compare viral vectors, lipid nanoparticles, polymeric polyplexes, calcium phosphate nanoparticles, and scaffold-integrated systems across transduction efficiency, expression kinetics, immunogenicity, and bone-site retention. We then examine how scaffold composition, architecture, and fabrication govern vector retention, release, and substrate-mediated transfection. This review then evaluates nucleic acid cargo selection and coordinated osteogenic and angiogenic gene delivery, including pDNA, mRNA, siRNA, miRNA, and explores emerging multi-factor, stimuli-responsive, and CRISPR-based GAMs alongside their translational constraints. A distinct feature of this review is its claim-level patent analysis, which identifies substantial intellectual-property white space in GAM development. Despite strong preclinical evidence, no GAM platform has simultaneously achieved scalable manufacturing, regulatory readiness as a combination product, and validation in a human-scale bone defect model. Clinical translation will require coordinated optimization of vector-scaffold interactions, manufacturing scalability, safety, and clinically relevant validation.

title: Nanotechnology-enabled construction of bispecific and multispecific antibody platforms for enhanced antitumor therapy
abstract: Refractory solid tumors are characterized by pronounced antigen heterogeneity, dense tissue barriers, and immunosuppressive microenvironments, which limit the tumor coverage and durable immune clearance achieved with conventional monospecific antibodies. Bispecific and multispecific antibodies (BsAbs and MsAbs) can recognize two or more antigens or epitopes, thereby integrating tumor targeting, immune-cell recruitment, and regulation of multiple signaling pathways within a single therapeutic system. However, soluble BsAbs and MsAbs remain limited by suboptimal circulatory stability, inadequate penetration and accumulation in solid tumors, limited control over antibody stoichiometry and spatial organization, and toxicities associated with systemic immune activation. Nanotechnology provides an engineering framework for addressing these limitations. Through chemical conjugation, affinity-tag-mediated assembly, anti-mPEG/mPEG anchoring, or Fc-mediated binding, nanocarriers can integrate multiple antibodies and therapeutic modules on a single platform while enabling multivalent display, oriented immobilization, and control over component ratios. Pharmacokinetics and tumor exposure can also be improved by nanoparticles; multivalent binding and immune-cell-tumor-cell bridging can be strengthened, and localized activation and combination therapy can be enabled through valency control, stimuli-responsive release, and co-delivery of therapeutic payloads. This review summarizes the principal construction strategies for nanotechnology-enabled BsAbs and MsAbs. It examines how these systems enhance binding avidity, improve in vivo delivery, increase therapeutic safety, and potentiate multimodal antitumor activity. Translational considerations, including quality control, immunogenicity, and scalable manufacturing, are discussed in the context of approved bispecific antibodies and early-phase clinical studies.
